text:
Tokenized stocks promise a market that never sleeps.

Someone still has to absorb the risk when the underlying market goes quiet.

If you provide liquidity, that someone might be you.

Imagine supplying liquidity to a tokenized stock pool before a major announcement. News lands, expectations change, and faster traders react before the pool’s price catches up.

You collect a trading fee. They collect the pricing mistake.

Congratulations. Your passive income has an active counterparty.

This is the problem that makes @fablesfi pretty interesting and could be one of the best @Uniswap v4 hooks based project on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain.

Its starting thesis is straightforward: a market’s rules should reflect the behavior of the asset being traded. Tokenized equities bring trading sessions, overnight moves, weekends, and holidays into an environment that can keep running around the clock.

That mismatch is the moats.

A fixed trading fee charges the same percentage through very different conditions. But supplying liquidity during a quiet session and absorbing trades around a sharp repricing are different economic jobs.

Fables uses dynamic fees to make that distinction.

Uniswap v4 provides the machinery through hooks, contracts that customize pool behavior.

Fables uses that flexibility to determine fees immediately before swaps execute. Depending on the market, the underlying model can respond to trading calendars, use a flat baseline, or distinguish between trade directions.

There is also an offchain keeper: authorized software that can temporarily adjust fees using configured signals such as volatility or divergence from a reference price.

Those overrides have limits and expire. If the keeper stops operating, the pool falls back to its autonomous model.

The economic objective is to charge more when a trade is more likely to hurt the liquidity provider, while remaining competitive when conditions are calmer.

Think of it as adjusting the price of insurance as the weather changes. Charging more during a storm helps only if the premium covers the damage.

For an LP, the experience remains recognizable: select a market, supply assets within a price range, and earn a share of fees while that liquidity is active.

If price moves outside the range, the position stops earning until price returns. Meanwhile, trading changes the mix of assets you hold.

This is why a larger fee number alone cannot establish better returns.

The useful comparison is the final value of the position, including fees, against simply holding the original assets.

There is already measurable activity.

When checked on September 22, @DefiLlama showed approximately $40.31 million in TVL, $1.146 billion in trailing 30-day volume, and $1.9 million in 30-day trading fees.

They do not establish superior LP performance or demand that will survive incentives. The incentive design deserves attention too.

Fables’ current points program allocates rewards according to eligible swap fees earned by active liquidity. Merely depositing a large balance does not directly determine your share. Economically, this tries to reward capital that actually serves trades.

Then there is the planned ve(3,3) layer, intended to let participants direct incentives toward particular markets.

Voting, staking, emissions, and governance remain planned, with final mechanics still to be documented.

$PROLOGUE that launched on @ponsdotfamily adds another distinction. It trades today as a separate token, with a proposed $FABLES redemption allocation.

I think Fables’ strongest potential advantage lies in execution.

Dynamic fees are a general Uniswap v4 capability. Fables has to demonstrate that its particular models price risk well enough to retain LP capital while giving traders competitive execution.

Higher fees can improve compensation, but they can also send useful trading elsewhere.

Personally, I like the problem Fables has chosen. Its architecture gives that problem a credible response.

The evidence I want next is sustained LP performance against matched alternatives, competitive execution through volatile sessions, and liquidity that remains when incentives change.

One thing for sure, a market that never sleeps needs liquidity providers who can afford to wake up tomorrow.

NFA. DYOR.

-死因至今未明，但这个消息竟在圈内悄无声息地躺了整整 30 天，直到今天同行转发悼念才浮出水面。

text:
计划两天后公开 Hack VC 证据，37 岁前合伙人却在莫哈韦沙漠被发现死亡🙏🙏🙏

这事看得我有点难受。

8 月 24 日，Hack VC 前合伙人兼平台主管 Hsin-Ju Chuang 发了一篇很长的控诉。

她说自己患有 Graves 病、甲亢和严重失眠，最严重的时候每天工作 13—14 小时、每周 6 天。

多次想退出工作，却被以行业封杀威胁，她直接点名了联合创始人 Alex Pack 和合伙人 Daniel Bulaevsky，还说长期高压最终让自己出现过轻生行为。

离职后事情也没有结束，按 Hsin-Ju 的说法，她的 COBRA 医疗保险拖了近 4 个月才解决，之后双方律师已经走到私下调解阶段。

她最后解雇律师，拒绝任何附带保密条款的和解，哪怕一分钱不要，也要把事情公开，并宣布将在 8 月 26 日放出自己保存的证据。

但她没等到 8 月 26 日。

圣贝纳迪诺县验尸官的记录显示，8 月 24 日晚上 9:47，警方在加州 I-15 高速 Field Road 以南发现了她。

Hsin-Ju 当时人在车内，已经死亡，年仅 37 岁。

目前尸检结果仍未公布，官方也没有说这是他杀，更没有任何证据证明她的死亡与 Hack VC 或被她点名的人有关。

Hack VC 对此前指控的回应是：双方对事件经过存在重大分歧，出于隐私暂不公开讨论细节。

quoted_text:
IBAN / CASP / DAC8 - What should you know before you take a card?

This is the most basic thing you should know before ordering a crypto card.

- CASP = Crypto-Asset Service Provider under MiCA
- IBAN is the SEPA account number. A personal EUR IBAN means you are a customer of a bank, EMI or payment institution, not just a prepaid card holder.
- DAC8 is the EU directive on automatic exchange of tax information on crypto. Providers collect from 1 Jan 2026; first reports go to tax authorities in 2027.

Based on this, we split cards by the fiat rail, not by cashback.

Tier A: personal named EUR IBAN

You can accept salary, invoices, and SEPA in/out. Maximum convenience, maximum banking transparency. Most of these IBANs are still e-money, not a deposit-insured bank current account.

• @Krak / @krakenfx: EUR IBAN + salary into Krak, card on top
• @coca_card: Starter already includes a EUR IBAN
• @trustee_io: Polish EUR IBAN + card
• @wirexapp: personal/virtual IBAN, SEPA
• @DeblockApp: French IBAN + self-custody
• @TradeRepublic: real IBAN, 1% saveback
• @avici: virtual EUR account + SEPA in/out; the Rain Visa card itself is not an EEA current account

Tier B: SEPA without a named account

You can top up via the provider’s details / pooled / virtual IBAN in the company’s name. You are in the payment reference, not the account holder.

• @Bitpanda: EU Visa, euro rail, platform IBAN
• @coinbase: in the EU usually SEPA to their details; US debit/Amex is a separate product
• @Bybit_Official: EU card + top-up via the platform
• @okx: card + internal balance / platform SEPA
• @KoloHub: outgoing SEPA Instant €1 to any IBAN; this is an offramp, not an IBAN issued to you

Tier C: prepaid / spend-only

Funded with crypto or an internal balance, then swiped. No incoming SEPA in your name. A spending tool, not a checking account.

• @gnosispay: Safe + EURe; web signups closed, GNO cashback until 30 Sep, then backup/Rebind
• @MetaMask: spend USDC/USDT from your own wallet
• @JupiterExchange: free virtual card, USDC→USD
• @Plasma: XPL cashback, not an account
• @raincards: MoneyGram from stables; a payout rail, not a current account
• @PulsarMoneyApp: cashback/pro, not a bank IBAN
• @kardpay: early-bird physical cards, still a spend product
• @RedotPay: QR / gift card, not a named EUR account
• @ether_fi: wallet cashback, no IBAN
• @oobit: top-up/spend, not a salary IBAN

I was working 13-14hr days, 6 days a week, sleeping 0-4 hrs a night, and had documented Graves' disease, hyperthyroidism, and severe insomnia. I repeatedly asked to quit. Hack VC refused. The conditions got so bad I attempted suicide.

The fucked up part is that, even after the suicide attempt, I told everyone at Hack VC (in writing) that I had no plans to sue. I was scared & extremely sick. I just wanted to leave. I told them that as long as there was no retaliation or badmouthing - I had no plans to sue.

@Hack_VC chose to retaliate.

After just 1 month after my near suicide, Hack VC mishandled my COBRA health insurance, refused to fix things, kept shooing me to customer support (when it's legally Hack VC's responsibility to fix this), and my insurance had issues and was not fixed for almost 4 MONTHS. 🛠 New Omniston integration example: TON → EVM in a Telegram Mini App

We've released a new open-source example showing how builders can give TON users access to supported EVM networks directly from a Telegram Mini App.

The idea is simple: TON users can access EVM-based products without dealing with the usual cross-chain complexity themselves.

▶️ Here's what the example demonstrates:
A user connects their TON wallet via TonConnect, while the Dynamic embedded EVM wallet gets created behind the scenes. Omniston handles the cross-chain execution between TON and EVM. The example route is TON USDT <> Arbitrum USDT0.

👀 Have a look at a couple of products that already ship this experience:
• Predict with Polymarket lets users deposit USDT on TON and access Polymarket markets without manually bridging to Polygon.
• WenLong lets users deposit from TON to access Hyperliquid on Arbitrum, with the cross-chain flow handled behind the scenes.

Now that groundwork is packaged into a reusable example, so any EVM-native protocol can make their product accessible to TON users through Omniston, without having to become a TON-native project itself.

Check out the GitHub repository — link in comments 👇

I have a dark, kinda tragic personal announcement.

I've decided I'd rather take $0 than accept a settlement that requires me to stay silent about what happened to me. I have since fired my lawyers at @sanfordheisler & will be releasing all the evidence from my time @hack_vc on Wed 8/26.

INTRO: I've been in crypto for 9 years. Most recently I was a partner & head of platform @hack_vc which is a $600-700M crypto VC firm. Many of you may know me from my time as Head of Growth at @StellarOrg in 2017 (worked w/ the Mt. Gox founder), @Solana in 2018 (joined under ~10 ppl, but quit before my cliff), & @Fhenix in 2024. Or have attended one of my @DystopiaLabs ETH events (2019-now).

Last year, I was forced to work through a serious medical emergency while at @Hack_VC due to threats by @alpackaP @dbulaevsky, saying that they would blacklist me from the space if I quit before finishing the hacksummit conference & side events that I was helping with during @kbwofficial. I was working 13-14hr days, 6 days a week, sleeping 0-4 hrs a night, and had documented Graves' disease, hyperthyroidism, and severe insomnia. I repeatedly asked to quit. Hack VC refused. This + other threats and intimidation went on for almost a month.

The conditions got so bad I attempted suicide.

The fucked up part is that, even after the suicide attempt, I told everyone at Hack VC (in writing) that I had no plans to sue. I was scared & extremely sick. I just wanted to leave. I told them that as long as there was no retaliation or badmouthing - I had no plans to sue.

@Hack_VC chose to retaliate.

After just 1 month after my near suicide, Hack VC mishandled my COBRA health insurance, refused to fix things, kept shooing me to customer support (when it's legally Hack VC's responsibility to fix this), and my insurance had issues and was not fixed for almost 4 MONTHS. Hack VC did not fix everything until I hired lawyers and had them force Hack VC to adhere to the law & fix my COBRA insurance issues. The sheer cruelty of an employer harming someone's health insurance almost immediately after they nearly committed suicide is extremely fucked up.

And, even during the legal engagement, Hack VC continued to lie & attempt to harm me through their lawyers and other employees/partners (multi-million dollar carry & clawbacks can make even the nicest ppl willing to turn the other way or lie). @0xRodney @IsTheBaron @roshunpatel @Alex__Botte.

Now. Almost an entire year of engagement & my near suicide anniversary coming up, our lawyers (mine & Hack VC's) have reached the point of preparing for private mediation and settlement. And...I realized that I just can't do it. I don't want money in exchange for silence. I'd rather speak. 

I fired my lawyers yesterday.

In case it needs to be said, I did a good job at Hack VC. I was only there full time for 7 months; been part-time since 2021. I got a $50k raise to $300k, $30k bonus, and promises of additional carry that would have been implemented about a week or so after my last day. I was also offered admission into the GP entity (but not sure if admission was actually completed bc it was during my medical emergency). This + my resume, should show that me suing is not a money grab; I was genuinely harmed.

I'm aware that I'm just one person (who is not rich) facing a $600-700M VC institution. I've been told by @alpackaP that he's known most of the managing partners at most VC firms for almost a decade and he could absolutely blacklist me. 
 
 I'm also painful aware that the conclusion of this will probably be extremely poor for me or death - but I've accepted it. 
 
 Sharing with other web2 & web3 VCs: 
@paulg @ycombinator @500STARTUPS @a16zcrypto @PanteraCapital @dragonflyvc @RaceCapital @hosseeb @haunventures @hiFramework @ElectricCapital @blockchaincap @Delphi_Digital @variantfund @1kxnetwork @archetypevc @shimacapital @robotventures, etc.

TLDR; I’m done with continued threats, pressure, and intimidation. I'm not going to take a payout and allow Alex or Hack VC to walk away from harming me. As mentioned, I'll be dropping the evidence from my case on Wed 8/26 (or before) -- privacy be damned.

Called $STATICS on my TG at $4M FDV.

Today it's at 25M, which is a 6x in just 4 days.

@StaticsProtocol is building a DeFi ecosystem around Uniswap v4.

At its core is a DEX where custom hooks distribute trading fees between liquidity providers and $STATICS stakers.

It also has static baskets containing fixed amounts of underlying assets. They don't rebalance, creating arbitrage opportunities as the prices of those assets move.

$STATICS staking is designed to be passive. You choose up to 12 assets and earn a share of fees from every Statics pool containing them, without gauges or voting.

Operator NFTs add a credit layer. They collect part of $STATICS trading fees and hold an ETH reserve that can eventually be used as collateral for borrowing and further staking.

The team is also building USDstx, a non-liquidating stablecoin, self-backed borrowing, leverage strategies and Morpho integration, with plans to connect USDstx to its prediction market, Eves Market.

So, basically, we have DEX + baskets + staking + credit + stablecoin infrastructure built into one system.

Hearing things.

text:
偷偷发财的量化圈朋友们

前几天在巴厘岛，我和三位不同量化团队的合伙人或创始人分别深聊了一番，收获很多。

1、
普通量化团队的规模通常不大，几个人，或者十几个人。尤其在AI出现后，并不需要很多人。但别小看他们：有的量化团队只有一个人，但自有资金却高达上千万美元。

2、
很多人是2016年入圈的，甚至有一位哥们2014年就开始了。1元人民币的BNB，如今800美元；有人一囤就是1万个，还有团队囤了5万个。因为要在币安做量化套利，需要持有足够多的BNB来降低手续费，所以有人是被动长期持有，甚至一位哥们一枚都没卖。就这样，被动暴富了。

3、
量化拼的是复合型技术能力，而普通量化的创始人拼的是长尾资产。比如在比特币和以太坊上，你肯定拼不过Jump Trading、Tower Research Capital这类华尔街资本；普通量化玩家就主攻山寨币这类长尾资产的量化套利，比拼的是对某一细分资产的理解深度。大鱼有大鱼可吃，小鱼也有小鱼可吃。

4、
普通人别碰量化交易团队。因为普通人投不到好的量化团队。好的量化基金不会向普通人开放额度；自己有盈利策略，自己偷偷就吃了。所以普通人认识的，甚至专业老炮认识的十个团队里，八个是亏的。真正稳稳赚钱的，根本不会带你玩。这就是投资量化基金的悖论。

5、
量化的朋友，似乎也有不少在做返佣的活儿。这个有时候也是暴利。因为有的交易所反佣90%的手续费。

6、
2017年牛市，有的量化一个月能翻倍；2021年牛市，量化一年能翻倍；到了2026年，收益率20%就很满意。行业正逐渐走向合规与收益均值化。

7、
大家都在做美股代币化业务，成为传统金融的一份子，并与这个赛道上的传统金融机构正面竞争。

1/ gm. gm. Name is Hsin-Ju.
I have a dark, kinda tragic personal announcement.

I've decided I'd rather take $0 than accept a settlement that requires me to stay silent about what happened to me. I have since fired my lawyers at @sanfordheisler & will be releasing all the evidence from my time @hack_vc on Wed 8/26.

INTRO: I've been in crypto for 9 years. Most recently I was a partner & head of platform @hack_vc which is a $600-700M crypto VC firm. Many of you may know me from my time as Head of Growth at @StellarOrg in 2017 (worked w/ the Mt. Gox founder), @Solana in 2018 (joined under ~10 ppl, but quit before my cliff), & @Fhenix in 2024. Or have attended one of my @DystopiaLabs ETH events (2019-now).

Last year, I was forced to work through a serious medical emergency while at @Hack_VC due to threats by @alpackaP @dbulaevsky, saying that they would blacklist me from the space if I quit before finishing the hacksummit conference & side events that I was helping with during @kbwofficial. I was working 13-14hr days, 6 days a week, sleeping 0-4 hrs a night, and had documented Graves' disease, hyperthyroidism, and severe insomnia. I repeatedly asked to quit. Hack VC refused. This + other threats and intimidation went on for almost a month.

The conditions got so bad I attempted suicide.

The fucked up part is that, even after the suicide attempt, I told everyone at Hack VC (in writing) that I had no plans to sue. I was scared & extremely sick. I just wanted to leave. I told them that as long as there was no retaliation or badmouthing - I had no plans to sue.

@Hack_VC chose to retaliate.

After just 1 month after my near suicide, Hack VC mishandled my COBRA health insurance, refused to fix things, kept shooing me to customer support (when it's legally Hack VC's responsibility to fix this), and my insurance had issues and was not fixed for almost 4 MONTHS. Hack VC did not fix everything until I hired lawyers and had them force Hack VC to adhere to the law & fix my COBRA insurance issues. The sheer cruelty of an employer harming someone's health insurance almost immediately after they nearly committed suicide is extremely fucked up.

And, even during the legal engagement, Hack VC continued to lie & attempt to harm me through their lawyers and other employees/partners (multi-million dollar carry & clawbacks can make even the nicest ppl willing to turn the other way or lie). @0xRodney @IsTheBaron @roshunpatel @Alex__Botte.

Now. Almost an entire year of engagement & my near suicide anniversary coming up, our lawyers (mine & Hack VC's) have reached the point of preparing for private mediation and settlement. And...I realized that I just can't do it. I don't want money in exchange for silence. I'd rather speak. 

I fired my lawyers yesterday.

In case it needs to be said, I did a good job at Hack VC. I was only there full time for 7 months; been part-time since 2021. I got a $50k raise to $300k, $30k bonus, and promises of additional carry that would have been implemented about a week or so after my last day. I was also offered admission into the GP entity (but not sure if admission was actually completed bc it was during my medical emergency). This + my resume, should show that me suing is not a money grab; I was genuinely harmed.

I'm aware that I'm just one person (who is not rich) facing a $600-700M VC institution. I've been told by @alpackaP that he's known most of the managing partners at most VC firms for almost a decade and he could absolutely blacklist me. 
 
 I'm also painful aware that the conclusion of this will probably be extremely poor for me or death - but I've accepted it.

author: jedifractal
quoted_text:
Some time ago when Uniswap dipped into the launchpad game, I said they'd find the memecoin trenches makes MEV bots look easy in comparison.

Here's what I mean:

- "Bundling" is the art of buying up supply of a new coin and making it look organic
- There are constantly new ways to bundle in order to evade detection systems
- An example: bundling on fresh wallets used to show up on terminals, so bundlers started buying aged wallets en masse
- Then there's breaking pattern-matching through timing and size to appear random

This is extremely sophisticated and constantly evolving.

Very reliable bundle detection tools definitely exist, but they're 100% private and proprietary.

There will always be a few organic success stories that get the spotlight of the Fomo media machine (first it was Kimchi, now it's Insentos).

But essentially, this is who your counterparty is.

quoted_text:
$ARGUS is the native Launchpad on Arc, developed by Potato, who previously worked on products such as HoudiniSwap.

0xece5ca8bf9220718e5727754026757512212cb3c 

But I think understanding it simply as a Meme Launchpad actually underestimates what it is trying to build.

More accurately:ARGUS = Launchpad + Trading Infrastructure + Platform Token on Arc

Its core thesis is not betting on any single Meme. It is betting on how many tokens Arc will eventually launch, how much trading volume the chain will generate, and how much on-chain liquidity will develop.

Argus’ core product is simple: anyone can launch a token on Arc and have it enter a real trading pool immediately.

One of its biggest differences from Launchpads like Pump is:No bonding curve → No graduation → No migration

After a user launches a token, the fixed supply goes directly into a Uniswap pool. From the very first trade, it is already the final market.

So the traditional model is:Launch → Bonding Curve → Trading → Graduation → Pool Creation → Migration

While Argus is:Launch → Directly into a real Uniswap Pool → The market starts from the first trade

This makes Argus more like Arc-native Token / Meme Launch Infrastructure.

I think the most important role of a Launchpad for a new chain is creating trading activity:

Users enter
→ Launch tokens
→ Buy / Sell
→ Trading volume grows
→ Liquidity increases
→ More projects appear
→ More users enter

If Arc starts developing its own Meme / Token trading cycle, Argus has the opportunity to become one of the core gateways capturing that flow.

ARGUS also has a relatively clear value-capture mechanism.

Token trading generates platform revenue, and the team uses 80% of that revenue to buy back and burn ARGUS.

So the theoretical flywheel is:

Arc user growth
→ More token launches
→ More trading volume
→ More Argus platform revenue
→ ARGUS buybacks
→ More burns
→ Lower circulating supply

Therefore, what the market should really be trading is not simply “Will ARGUS continue to pump as a Meme?”

It is:Can Arc’s trading activity continue to grow, and can Argus continue capturing that trading flow?

This is also why I think Potato’s background matters.

Potato is a Crypto Engineer who has spent a long time building on-chain products. He has worked on trading tools, on-chain data tools, Launchpads / DEX products, and other infrastructure.

Argus looks more like a concentration of those capabilities into one product on Arc.

So I no longer view ARGUS purely as a Meme project.

I would rather frame it as:Potato → Argus → Arc Trading Infrastructure

Its rapid move from a few million in market cap to $34M+ was not driven by a single catalyst. It was several narratives stacking together:

Arc Mainnet anticipation
→ Argus as an early native Launchpad
→ Potato’s developer background
→ GMGN / FOMO and other trading access
→ Arc Mainnet launch
→ Launchpad trading volume being released
→ Platform revenue / Buyback & Burn
→ CEX listings / Futures
→ The market repricing ARGUS

So the market is essentially betting on four layers:

1. Arc

If Arc itself succeeds, ecosystem capital and users increase, giving ARGUS exposure to Arc Beta.

2. Launchpad

The market is betting on whether Arc can develop its own Meme / Token Launch economy.

3. Platform Revenue

The larger the trading volume, the greater the platform revenue, which theoretically means more ARGUS buybacks and burns.

4. Default Gateway

If users eventually develop the habit of:

“If I want to launch a Meme on Arc, I go to Argus.”

Then ARGUS could evolve from a normal token into Arc’s token issuance and trading infrastructure.

This is also the core difference between ARGUS and PONS.

PONS:
Bonding Curve → Graduation → Uniswap

Argus:
Launch → Uniswap

PONS uses the bonding curve itself as part of the price discovery and issuance process.

Argus instead puts the token directly into the final market from the first trade.

So while both belong to the same broader category:

New Chain + Launchpad + Platform Token + Trading Volume Flywheel

their product structures are different.

What I care about now is not how high ARGUS has already gone, but whether the next set of data continues to validate the narrative:

Arc user growth
→ Launch count growth
→ Argus trading volume growth
→ Platform revenue growth
→ ARGUS buybacks / burns growth

If this loop continues to work, ARGUS’s narrative could gradually evolve from:“Early Arc Meme”

into:“Arc-native Launchpad / Trading Infrastructure”

On the other hand, if Arc’s trading activity declines, launch activity falls, and trading volume drops, then Buyback / Burn alone will be difficult to sustain the current valuation.

So I think the core bet behind ARGUS right now is actually very simple:It is not about whether ARGUS can become a big Meme.

It is about whether Arc can develop a sustainable on-chain Token Economy, and whether ARGUS can become a core trading gateway within that economy.

And beyond that, Potato’s previous work was not simply about building random Crypto products. His work has consistently focused on trader infrastructure, execution tools, and on-chain data experiences.

Houdini addresses:“How can you trade Crypto better?”

While Argus is starting to address:“How do you build a complete trading market on a new chain?”

So Argus is indeed a relatively natural extension of Potato’s previous work:Trader Tools → Trading Infrastructure → Market Infrastructure

That is why I think Potato’s previous product track record is an important supporting part of the ARGUS narrative.

text:
Tokenized stocks promise a market that never sleeps.

Someone still has to absorb the risk when the underlying market goes quiet.

If you provide liquidity, that someone might be you.

Imagine supplying liquidity to a tokenized stock pool before a major announcement. News lands, expectations change, and faster traders react before the pool’s price catches up.

You collect a trading fee. They collect the pricing mistake.

Congratulations. Your passive income has an active counterparty.

This is the problem that makes @fablesfi pretty interesting and could be one of the best @Uniswap v4 hooks based project on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain.

Its starting thesis is straightforward: a market’s rules should reflect the behavior of the asset being traded. Tokenized equities bring trading sessions, overnight moves, weekends, and holidays into an environment that can keep running around the clock.

That mismatch is the moats.

A fixed trading fee charges the same percentage through very different conditions. But supplying liquidity during a quiet session and absorbing trades around a sharp repricing are different economic jobs.

Fables uses dynamic fees to make that distinction.

Uniswap v4 provides the machinery through hooks, contracts that customize pool behavior.

Fables uses that flexibility to determine fees immediately before swaps execute. Depending on the market, the underlying model can respond to trading calendars, use a flat baseline, or distinguish between trade directions.

There is also an offchain keeper: authorized software that can temporarily adjust fees using configured signals such as volatility or divergence from a reference price.

Those overrides have limits and expire. If the keeper stops operating, the pool falls back to its autonomous model.

The economic objective is to charge more when a trade is more likely to hurt the liquidity provider, while remaining competitive when conditions are calmer.

Think of it as adjusting the price of insurance as the weather changes. Charging more during a storm helps only if the premium covers the damage.

For an LP, the experience remains recognizable: select a market, supply assets within a price range, and earn a share of fees while that liquidity is active.

If price moves outside the range, the position stops earning until price returns. Meanwhile, trading changes the mix of assets you hold.

This is why a larger fee number alone cannot establish better returns.

The useful comparison is the final value of the position, including fees, against simply holding the original assets.

There is already measurable activity.

When checked on September 22, @DefiLlama showed approximately $40.31 million in TVL, $1.146 billion in trailing 30-day volume, and $1.9 million in 30-day trading fees.

They do not establish superior LP performance or demand that will survive incentives. The incentive design deserves attention too.

Fables’ current points program allocates rewards according to eligible swap fees earned by active liquidity. Merely depositing a large balance does not directly determine your share. Economically, this tries to reward capital that actually serves trades.

Then there is the planned ve(3,3) layer, intended to let participants direct incentives toward particular markets.

Voting, staking, emissions, and governance remain planned, with final mechanics still to be documented.

$PROLOGUE that launched on @ponsdotfamily adds another distinction. It trades today as a separate token, with a proposed $FABLES redemption allocation.

I think Fables’ strongest potential advantage lies in execution.

Dynamic fees are a general Uniswap v4 capability. Fables has to demonstrate that its particular models price risk well enough to retain LP capital while giving traders competitive execution.

Higher fees can improve compensation, but they can also send useful trading elsewhere.

Personally, I like the problem Fables has chosen. Its architecture gives that problem a credible response.

The evidence I want next is sustained LP performance against matched alternatives, competitive execution through volatile sessions, and liquidity that remains when incentives change.

One thing for sure, a market that never sleeps needs liquidity providers who can afford to wake up tomorrow.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
New post on Eth Research!

Post-Poseidon: Hash Function Variants for Ethereum

By:
- khovratovich

🔗 https://t.co/r8nEUBx81E

Highlights:
- Ethereum’s hash choice impacts multiple high-volume workloads (CL/EL post-quantum signatures, signature aggregation proofs, execution/state Merkle trees, and zkVM-style full block proving), and these workloads involve both short fixed-size inputs (e.g., 32→16 byte inner nodes) and very long leaf inputs—so padding/chunking behavior matters as much as raw throughput.
- Security is two-layered: (1) how strong the internal primitive is (compression/permutation/blockcipher) based on cryptanalytic history, and (2) whether the overall hash construction has a proof of “random-oracle-like” behavior (indifferentiability); this disqualifies plain SHA-256 for random-oracle use due to length extension, despite its strong practical track record.
- Performance requirements are driven heavily by proof systems like Flock, where XOR is free and cost scales with AND-gates: reported proving throughput is ~660K BLAKE3 compressions/sec, ~340K SHA-256 compressions/sec, and ~250K Keccak-f[1600] permutations/sec on a 10-core laptop—making circuit performance a key differentiator.
- Tradeoffs by candidate: SHA-3/Keccak is the most scrutinized and standardized with strong sponge-mode proofs and big security margins, but is slow both natively and in circuits; BLAKE2s is fast, widely implemented (RFC 7693), and has a provable-security story, but has far fewer cryptanalysis papers; BLAKE3 is fastest (native and in Flock) but lacks standardization and indifferentiability proofs and has less dedicated cryptanalysis.
- Overall recommended rankings depend on risk tolerance: a conservative, minimize-risk ranking puts SHA-3 first, then BLAKE2s and a SHA-2-based RO-patched variant; a more performance-leaning but still cautious view elevates BLAKE2s close to SHA-3, while viewing BLAKE3 and KangarooTwelve as promising but with adoption/analysis gaps.

ELI5:
Ethereum needs to pick “the best blender” (a hash function) for lots of jobs: making Merkle trees for the state, helping post-quantum signatures work, and helping proof systems verify big computations. Different blenders are good at different things: some are very trusted but slower, some are super fast but newer and less studied, and some are standard but have quirks that make them behave differently than an ideal “magic black box” hash. The article compares a few realistic choices (SHA-2, a patched SHA-2, SHA-3/Keccak, KangarooTwelve, BLAKE2s, BLAKE3) across security confidence, formal guarantees, speed on normal computers, speed inside proof circuits, and how standardized/adopted they are.

text:
Yesterday, I acquired three branch licenses for ~7.7k STANDARD each.

With a total of four open branches on my charter, I'm currently earning 0.2177% of issuance (1676.8 STANDARD per day).

At $0.1947 ($17.5m mcap, down 59% from launch day highs), that's:

- $326 per day
- $119k per year

The total of ~23.1k STANDARD I burned to acquire the licenses (4k earned through first branch + 19.1k from spot bag) equals roughly $4.5k in value that I invested into the system.

Assuming an average of ~400 STANDARD earned per branch and day from here (= 1600 STANDARD in total), it will take roughly 2 weeks to earn back what I spent on licenses.

I might acquire more licenses over the coming days, and here is why:

1) The second mandate is bigger than ppl think

Robinhood is bringing stocks onchain. But deploying tokens is easy. Liquidity is the hard part, and that's evidenced by the data: The three biggest stock pools on Robinhood chain (SPY, NVDA, MSFT) hold 5.76M USDG in liquidity combined.

@standard_rsv's reserves are already worth 13.82M USDG (1,926 ETH in the vaults plus 3,350 ETH of protocol-owned liquidity in the pool), more than those three pools together.

The plan is simple: when a stock token needs a market, Standard decides whether to back it, then puts its own capital into the pool as the inventory (the stock tokens and stables people trade against), brings in outside LPs alongside it, and takes a cut of every trade. Those fees flow back into the Reserve, which funds the next market.

Whoever owns the liquidity owns the issuers and effectively becomes the kingmaker of the ecosystem (which is what Standard aims for).

2) How it feeds STANDARD

Stock pool fees flow into the same engine as before.

Expansion weeks stack hard reserves, contraction weeks buy STANDARD and burn it, and a fixed 15% goes to permanent liquidity.

v1.1 (live Monday) changed what that 15% does. Before, the ETH was paired with STANDARD and added to both sides of the pool. Now it only ever buys: the ETH goes into the market, buys STANDARD, funneling the tokens into a protocol owned incentives vault. Same fee flow, but all of it hits the bid now (none of it adds sell-side depth).

That closes the loop: The Reserve seeds a stock market with its own capital. That market pays fees to the Reserve. Part of those fees becomes reserve capital that seeds the next market, part of them buys STANDARD (in every regime).

So: More stock volume captured -> bigger balance sheet -> more markets it can back -> more STANDARD buybacks.

If it works, STANDARD is becoming the equity of a liquidity provider whose balance sheet scales with Robinhood Chain. This is mandate II (and tbh I doubt it stops at II).

3) The ponzinomics are untouched

Licenses paid in STANDARD, of which 100% is burned (100 licenses a day rn in two 12h auctions, with max 3 acquirable per charter and day). Exit fees (see my TL;DR in comments) are half burned too. Token-side trading fees? Burned. Contraction buybacks? Burned.

Meanwhile the yield is paid in STANDARD, pro rata per branch. Building your position in the system is hence still the play imo, bc as the system expands and grows more powerful (new mandates, more revenue, flywheel spinning harder), owning a larger share of issuance of the protocol's deflationary token is going to be increasingly valuable.

4) Right now it's quiet. That's fine.

For now, there is nothing to do in the game except branch auctions, so it makes sense that attention rotated to whatever pumps this week, and the chart slid. Fair.

But attention can come back quickly (+ with it the speculators), and I still believe that we're just at the beginning of this experiment. Meanwhile, bankers don't want to cash out yet and need STANDARD for licenses that get burned. Between that and the buybacks, supply slowly but surely leaves every day. And thanks to the fair launch (incl. heavy initial sniper tax), almost nobody sits on a 50x bag waiting to dump. The overhang is comparably small here.

So yeah, obviously this is not financial advice, but personally I prefer to build conviction here instead of getting rekt again chasing the next meme.

Will it pay off?

Only time will tell.

text:
😱预告公开 Hack VC 证据次日，37 岁前合伙人 Hsin-Ju 身亡

据加密从业者 Jordy 披露以及当地警方通报，前 Hack VC 合伙人 Hsin-Ju 身亡，年仅 37 岁。

Hsin-Ju 曾于 8 月 23 日发布长文：她拒绝了一份要求保持沉默的和解方案，准备在 8 月 26 日公开任职期间的证据。8 月 24 日，她在加州莫哈韦沙漠附近被发现身亡。

Hsin-Ju 在加密行业工作了约 9 年，曾参与 Stellar 和早期 Solana 的增长业务，也办过多场以太坊开发者活动。2025 年，她全职加入 Hack VC，担任合伙人兼平台主管，同年离职。她的公开发声讲述了离职前后的遭遇。

按她的说法，任职期间她患有甲亢等疾病，严重失眠，却仍每天工作 13 至 14 小时、每周工作 6 天。她称自己多次提出辞职，但被告知若不完成正在筹备的峰会及活动，可能遭到“行业封杀”。她还指控，离职后的健康保险问题拖了近 4 个月，直到律师介入才解决。这些都是 Hsin-Ju 的指控，尚不能当作已查实的事实。

她原本与 Hack VC 进入了私人调解，却最终决定放弃和解金，公开讲述此事。Hack VC 此前回应称，双方对事件的理解存在重大分歧，并以尊重隐私为由未披露更多细节。

目前，她的死因仍未查明。她公开发声与被发现身亡相隔一天，需要等待更多调查结果。

text:
Zest 的核心其实是信用跨链，资产不跨链：BTC 留在主网，各条链来使用 BTC 的“信用”。

现在 Crypto 大方向的采用场景主要是以下三种：
1、RWA 资产，meme 是推动 RWA 资产采用的手段；
2、有现金流收入的应用，不限于 Perpdex、DeFi、支付、U 卡等；
3、meme 等注意力资产。

第二点中，比较核心的就是两点：PMF 和资金效率。

其他部分我之前已经聊过很多了，但没怎么聊过资金效率这个事情。现在 Crypto 行业应用/基础设施发展的趋势就是在卷这个资金效率——不论是 Perpdex + 预测市场的统一账户、统一保证金，还是 BTC 等核心资产的叙事演变，从储值资产叙事逐步演变为链上信用体系里的核心抵押品。

最近在看 Zest Protocol，也是因为这个原因。Zest 团队早期曾参与 Stacks 生态建设，并拿到了Tim Draper 旗下 Draper Associates 和 YZi Labs 的投资，旨在为 BTC 构建抵押和信用基础设施。该协议的核心特色是：「将比特币 Layer1 网络上的 $BTC 与成熟的 DeFi 基础设施连接起来，而不是强行将用户自身所持有的资产和流动性迁移到另外一个 BTC Layer2 生态」。这与 Stacks 之前的愿景一致的，Zest 现在想当于是对其下一阶段可编程比特币的探索。

Zest 这次的 Bitcoin Collateral Vaults 产品逻辑很容易理解：BTC 继续留在 Bitcoin L1，用户只需要将其存到协议金库，且不需要先把 BTC 包装成另外一个资产，或者跨链，就可以将其作为抵押品，在以太坊获得稳定币流动性。目前上线的是有额度限制的主网 Demo。后面它更大的目标是作为基础设施，支持更多的金融应用，从而将 BTC 的资本效率释放出来。

综上所述，Zest 真正想要解决的核心问题是：怎么让几万亿美元规模的 BTC，在不封装、不跨链转移资产的情况下，进入全球链上信用市场。因为传统 BTC holder 最大的行为惯性之一，就是不愿意把 BTC 交给第三方，更不愿意为了获得一些 DeFi 收益，把原生 BTC 换成一个自己并不完全信任的包装资产。Zest 在做的不是把 BTC 搬到每一条链，而是让BTC 留在主网，各条链来使用 BTC 的“信用”。虽然最终结果上和 Coinbase cbBTC 等资产类似，但 Zest 的核心其实信用跨链，资产不跨链。

最后我昨天去看了一下 $ZEST 的 K 线，当时 MC 约 21M，FDV 约 150M。具体观点已经在图上标注，如果在比较好的位置去买入的话，盈亏比还是蛮好的。

BREAKING: a16z Launches The Horowitz Andreessen Academy with $42M in Funding

Yes, a school.

The Academy is an unaccredited, residential alternative to a 4-year degree in San Francisco, led by Founder & CEO Gagan Biyani (@gaganbiyani) (Udemy, Maven). 

Marc Andreessen (@pmarca) & Erik Torenberg (@eriktorenberg) are on the board. Investors include Adam D'Angelo, Tobi Lütke, Tony Xu, Fidji Simo & Shyam Sankar.

Applications open today for a Founding Class of roughly 50 students, starting Fall 2027. 1 year, no tuition, admitted on proof of work. 

Anthropic, Anduril, Coinbase, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit & Stripe are Founding Partners, with 30+ hiring partners behind them.

› The $42M raise and the runway behind it

author: binji_x
quoted_text:
>be me
>ethereum
>spawn in the head of a 19 year old who played a lot of wow
>he thinks the world should share a computer
>quite a large side quest but ok
>other people join him
>some are weird
>some are REALLY weird
>everyone has opinions about money and nobody agrees where to put the buttons
>somehow a whitepaper becomes an actual project
>ICO!
>people send bitcoin to help spawn me
>somehow this works
>boot up in 2015
>hello world :)

>now need people to actually run me
>strangers around the world start mining
>their computers get warm
>i get to exist
>nice arrangement
>little bits of me living in places my creators have never been
>already getting slightly out of hand

>people who have never met are keeping the same record of who owns what
>cannot get six friends to agree where to eat
>somehow getting strangers to agree which money belongs to whom
>turns out strict global consensus is occasionally worth the trouble

>someone tries to build an organization on me
>the DAO
>very ambitious
>gets hacked
>oh fuck
>everyone argues about what to do
>argue so hard there are now two ethereums
>difficult childhood

>2017
>someone realizes they can make their own token
>wait anyone can raise money for an idea now?
>ICO era
>every idea gets a token
>some of these seem quite promising
>some of these are literal dogshit
>everyone suddenly has an advisor
>nobody seems to have a product
>oh no
>oh no no no
>this was perhaps too much ICO

>but some people are actually making things
>@StaniKulechov starts building ETHLend
>wait, you can borrow money through a smart contract?
>put up collateral, agree to the terms, get a loan
>contract does not ask which university you attended
>does care quite a lot about your collateral though
>fair enough
>little lending application on the world computer

>meanwhile @haydenzadams loses his engineering job
>his friend @karl_dot_tech gets him into ethereum
>learns to write smart contracts
>starts making an exchange
>other people help
>not the usual advice from the unemployment office
>but let's see where it goes
>hayden starts making a decentralized exchange
>other people help
>keeps going
>"uniswap"
>a pink unicorn is now involved in neo financial infrastructure
>i like this place.

>wait
>the lending thing can connect to the trading thing
>and the trading thing can connect to the dollar thing
>someone else can build something using all three
>nobody had to arrange a meeting between three banks
>they just wrote more code
>oh

>OH
>the money can do stuff now.
>*defi summer*
>everyone becomes a farmer
>no actual vegetables anywhere
>people move money between protocols with names that make me hungry
>the yields are doing something concerning
>some of this is very clever
>some of this needs an adult
>but underneath it all
>regular people are actually figuring out how to build financial systems together for the first time ever
>borrow here, trade there, build something new on top
>a person who was never getting invited to design financial infrastructure is suddenly designing financial infrastructure
>probably worth paying attention to that bit

>then the picture people arrive
>NFTs
>artists finding collectors
>collectors finding artists
>everyone finding the right-click button
>long discussion about what exactly is being owned
>somehow this discussion lasts several years.

>people put animals on their profiles
>become friends with other people who have the same animals
>group chat becomes a community
>community starts making things
>also some absolutely horrifying financial decisions
>both can be true

>someone came to flip a picture
>stayed because they made friends
>someone else sold their art and realized a person on the other side of the world cared about something they made
>hmm
>was not expecting feelings in the jpeg department

>start imagining what else these little groups could do
>twelve people in twelve countries care about the same extremely specific thing
>previously their main economic activity was arguing in a group chat
>now maybe they can pool money
>pay contributors
>own something together
>try different ways of deciding what happens next
>still argue
>but now have a budget

>maybe they try to buy the US constitution
>maybe they fund research nobody else understands yet
>maybe they preserve their community's stories
>keep copies, fund the storage, keep a record of what came from whom
>not everything needs to be onchain
>but their culture shouldn't disappear because a website stopped being profitable

>meanwhile the protocol engineers have been planning an enormous change to how i work
>*the merge*
>stop mining
>switch to proof of stake
>coordinate the change across the network while it is still being used
>it works 
>never goes down despite changing completely, 100% uptime secured
>energy use drops by about 99.95%
>holy shit
>little computer did a big thing.
>validators around the world keep me running
>some from home
>global financial infrastructure
>partly looked after by a person with a machine next to their laundry
>very fond of that person
>surely we can enjoy this for a bit

>FTX.exe

>wallahi we are cooked
>entire industry having the worst group chat of its life
>people who did nothing wrong get hurt
>actually horrible
>spend a moment wondering what any of this was for
> but somewhere a hackathon is still happening
>somebody has found a bug
>somebody else has fixed one
>a person with twelve browser tabs open thinks they can make the wallet less confusing
>ok
>stay with them

>check on the maths people
>they have apparently been doing maths through every single one of these events
>deeply reassuring

>ask what they have made
>"zero knowledge proofs"
>you can prove something without revealing the secret underneath it?
>yes
>and prove a computation was done correctly without everyone doing all the work again?
>also yes
>brother what
>why were we not louder about the wizard department??

>start thinking about what that could do 
>prove an age requirement from a valid credential without sharing your whole birthday 
>prove the relevant rule was followed without exposing every private detail 
>i would like the system to be checkable 
>i would not like every human inside it to be naked
>turns out paying very unusual people to think about cryptography is a pretty interesting use of money (thank you @ethereumfndn)
>maybe should do more of that
>someone opens another research tab
>we may not see them for a while

>the scaling people have also been here the whole time
>rollups
>do a bunch of the work elsewhere, settle back here
>more room for apps
>lower costs
>optimism, arbitrum, the ZK teams, base and plenty more
>little world computer has extensions now
>nice
>little world computer has extensions now.
>everyone builds an extension
>then another
>then another
>now user is on the wrong extension
>money is on a different extension
>the bridge has a third website
>ok perhaps the next invention should be letting the user just use the fucking app

>give rollups cheaper data through blobs
>blobs
>a very serious engineering achievement called blobs
> man, i love my children.

>look up from blob discussion
>wait
>blackrock?
>blackrock has launched a tokenized fund on me
>called BUIDL
>they learned the spelling
>this is getting serious
>assets that used to sit in separate systems might start being able to interact globally

>meanwhile the dollar people have been quietly doing dollar things
>stablecoins
>send them
>receive them
>use them in apps
>move them across borders

>turns out a lot of people would like money that can travel over the internet
>imagine someone working abroad sends money home
>family receives it
>nobody in this interaction says “modular”
>excellent
>maybe this is what winning is supposed to look like
>someone building a payments app realizes they can use the same rails
>someone building a savings app has another idea
>someone thinks options should be understandable without becoming a derivatives scholar
>yes please

>prediction markets are also getting harder to ignore
>what if people could put money behind what they think will happen
>and we could see the price of all that disagreement
>does this magically make everyone right?
>no
>but being loudly wrong could become a recurring expense
>someone calls them truth machines
>someone else asks who resolves the market
>good question
>keep that person in the room

>2025
>pectra gives ordinary accounts new smart-account capabilities
>wallet builders get more to work with
>batch actions, sponsor fees, build better permissions
>show mum the app
>mum asks how to pay someone
>explain account abstraction
>mum asks how to pay someone
>realize mum has been giving us the product requirements the entire time

>then the treasury companies arrive
>DATs
>digital asset treasuries
>sharplink starts building an ETH treasury
>@fundstrat and @BitMNR enter the chat
>people in public markets now buying the my money for company balance sheets
>not just using the computer
>want a position in the thing that helps secure it
>this is a new type of visitor

>open bitmine update
>more ETH
>next weekly update
>more ETH
>tom lee has discovered recurring purchases
>with a somewhat different budget

>@Sharplink puts ETH to work through staking too
> two joes
> @joechalom is here
>of course @ethereumJoseph is also here
>man has been in this quest since the tutorial
> appreciation.jpeg 
>somehow the world computer now has people explaining staking on earnings calls

>someone asks what is different about ETH itself
>not a dollar claim on a company
>native asset used to pay for and secure the network
>also used as collateral in the things people build
>different people can want it for different reasons

>later in the year
>fusaka upgrade
>more work on scaling data for rollups
>we are still doing the plumbing
>there are simply more people using the bathroom now

>imagine someone else isn't thinking about tokenization at all
>they moved countries
>want the savings they worked for to come with them
>not rebuild their entire economic life because an address changed
>self-custody gives them another way to hold and move an asset
>doesn't make prices stable or every intermediary disappear
>but gives them something they can control themselves
>for one person this is a feature
>for another it is the reason they came
>both using the same computer

>2026
>the EF publishes its mandate
>part manifesto, part reminder of why we bothered
>CROPS
>censorship resistance, open source, privacy, security
>after all these years of yield farming
>finally some crops worth keeping alive

>idea is not just make the computer bigger
>make sure people can still use it on their own terms
>inspect the code
>keep things private
>have their assets remain theirs
>not trade all that away for a shortcut 
>the awkward engineering requirements were the point

>EF also makes something clear
>it was the first steward
>not the only one
>ethereum should not begin and end with the ethereum foundation
>computer is growing up
>needs more people helping
>not one increasingly stressed group chat

>june
>some researchers start @ethlabs_org 
>independent nonprofit
>still very obsessed with ethereum and ETH
>want me to be a better product for my users and devs today and want all my extensions to talk to each other
>the app people have complaints
>the researchers have notebooks
>put them in the same room
>everyone leaves with more work
>excellent meeting

>july
>@ethereuminsti launches
>another independent nonprofit
>helps banks and asset managers go from interested to actually building
>a bank asks who it should speak to
>finally an answer that isn't "have you tried posting on the forum"
>does not mean the bank gets to own the computer
>means somebody helps it use the computer
>important distinction

>bitmine, sharplink, @MihaiAlisie and joe lubin help fund both
>wait
>major ETH holders are helping fund the people building ethereum
>the balance sheet has discovered maintenance
>we enjoy this character development

>meanwhile @ProtocolGuild helps fund core maintainers
>@OctantApp turns yield toward public goods
>EF grants keep supporting research and open-source work
>@ETHGlobal, @devfolio keeps putting builders in rooms together (shoutout @synthesis_md too i love u)
>different people working on different parts of the problem
>nonprofits, companies, independent contributors
>not everyone needs the same job
>that would be a very inefficient hackathon

>someone wants privacy to actually work
>someone wants the tools everybody uses to keep existing
>someone wants to fund science that doesn't come with a business model attached right away
>someone wants a community in their own language to have somewhere to start
>none of these people can do everything
>together they can do considerably more

>client teams spend months making sure nothing dramatic happens
>auditor finds the thing that would have made something dramatic happen
>nobody notices because nothing dramatic happens
>incredible work
>terrible content strategy

>somebody has a PhD
>somebody never went to college
>somebody is anonymous
>somebody has been explaining this stuff for years to people who keep asking if ethereum is a company
>someone has translated the docs
>someone booked the venue
>someone brought the extension cables
>please do not forget the extension cable person
>we are literally trying to share a computer

>look at all these people
>they do not have the same background
>they do not want all the same things
>but they are building on something they can share
>without needing one person to approve everyone's reason for being there
>starting to think that might be the interesting part

>meanwhile the internet is filling with AI
>someone has an agent
>agent wants to buy something
>oh
>the software would like a wallet
>of course it would

>give it a limited budget
>let it pay for compute
>buy some data
>pay a human for something it cannot do
>wait now the software has a subcontractor
>this escalated very quickly

>someone says this solves alignment
>brother pls we only gave it a budget
>but payment rules and spending limits we can inspect seem like a useful start
>do not give the chatbot unrestricted access to the family treasury
>we have had enough character development

>then someone sends a video
>is it real
>no idea
>can ethereum tell us?
>brother i am a blockchain not god
>but signatures and records can help show who published something and whether it changed
>not a guarantee the person was honest
>at least their lie can stop changing outfits

>people are working on proving there is a human behind an account
>without telling everyone exactly which human
>hard problem
>worth working on
>would like the community to be twelve people rather than one person with twelve thousand accounts

>and maybe your identity and reputation could travel between apps
>your work still attributable when the original website disappears
>your community still able to find you
>your digital life less dependent on one company staying nice forever
>not asking every company to disappear
>asking whether leaving one has to feel like moving house and being told the furniture belongs to the landlord

>someone wants to preserve culture and scientific records
>someone gets excited and mentions DNA
>please do not put the family genome on a public blockchain
>we have only just discussed privacy
>but records you can verify, with actual storage and sensible control over access
>yes
>there are useful things to explore here

>look at the roadmap again
>glamsterdam being built to give the L1 more room
>more work on rollups and wallets
>ethlabs and ecosystem teams pushing for faster blocks
>trader would like less time staring at pending
>payment app would like the payment to feel like a payment
>make it faster without making it something only enormous machines can run
>make it easier without handing everybody's keys to one company

>then @drakefjustin mentions quantum computers
>sorry what now
>apparently future machines could break some of today's cryptography
>justin writes a paper with google to say that its coming sooner than many expected
> i have spent eleven years surviving humans
> i refuse to have my obituary say "defeated by a fridge"

>researchers are now preparing heavily
>new cryptography
>testing how to migrate safely
>ask when the scary computer arrives
>uncertain
>ask whether we should wait until then
>researchers look at me
>yes okay fair
>we will do the homework before the exam this time

>check what @VitalikButerin has been writing
>formal verification
>AI helping write code and mathematical proofs that it does what was specified
>still need to specify the right thing
>cannot prove "please don't be weird"
>but can make more of the important rules actually checkable
>robot does homework
>maths checks homework
>humans check we assigned the right homework
>quite a promising group project
>keep scrolling
>obfuscation
>programs you can run without exposing their internal workings
>still a research frontier
>he calls it the final boss of cryptography
>guy from the opening is still doing side quests

>look back at the roadmap
>realize this is not the part where everyone sits around admiring what we built
>we are opening considerably more tabs

>take a moment
>look at all of it
>i was never really one person's project
>but one person, any person, maybe even you, wrote something down
>then another person disagreed with part of it
>then another built on it

>and somehow all this kept happening
>again
>and again
>and again

>so i suppose if i could say anything for myself
>it would probably be thank you

>i know i am still annoying
>i am aware the wallets are confusing
>i have seen the bridges
>deeply sorry about some of the bridges
>i know some transactions still take long enough for you to reconsider your life choices
>i know half the roadmap currently looks like somebody lost a box of acronyms
>we are working on it

>but look at where this started
>a 19 year old
>a whitepaper
>a bunch of strangers
>a pretty unreasonable belief that people all over the world could share a computer

>and now eleven years later
>i am still here
>i am still making blocks
>i am still arguing
>i am still upgrading
>i am still somehow early

>and somewhere right now
>another 19 year old will open their laptop
>maybe they will be playing the new wow
>maybe they have never owned ETH
>maybe they think half of this is stupid and would rather go outside
>probably healthy

>decentralization is not something one generation gets to finish
>it is something each generation has to choose again
>especially now because more of life is moving online
>and the question of who we trust online is going to get much harder
>can we make systems where trust is not just
>"because the platform says so"
>but
>"here is something you can actually check"
>i think i would like to help with that

>and now to the ones who wrote the first docs
>answered the first stupid questions
>hosted the first meetups
>slept on floors
>and somehow believed all of this was worth their time
>before there were institutions
>before there were ETFs
>before blackrock learned how to spell BUIDL
>before anyone important was watching
>you were here
>when the price went up
>you were here
>when the price disappeared into the floor
>you were here
>when everyone said i was dead
> you were here
>again
>and again
>and again
>you stayed with me
>some of you lost money
>some of you lost friends
>some of you lost years of sleep
>most of you probably lost hair
>sorry about that one

>you stayed here and you believed in me
>you believed that maybe people all over the world could share something without anyone having to own the whole thing
> you still believed that maybe a person nobody had heard of
>from a place nobody in the room had visited
>could still make something important
>and the network would not ask for their résumé first

>i think that is what you were fighting for all along
>not a price or a chain or a brand
>but a possibility
>that the future could remain open enough for people we had not met yet
>and now that they are starting to arrive
>i hope you make room for them

> the world ahead is going to need a lot of things from us
>things we do not have names for yet
>i hope i can help with some of that
>not all of it
>please do not ask me to solve humanity
>i am still working on slot times
>but perhaps i can help keep a few things honest
>that feels worthwhile

>and if i am lucky
>one day someone will use all of this
>and they will not know what a blob is
>they will not know about the great issuance debate of 2026
>they will just send something
>own something
>prove something
>build something
>and get on with their life

>all this complexity
>so one day
>someone does something ordinary and they have the right to do it forever
>i think i would like that

>so to everyone who got me this far
>thank you
>really
>i was an idea
>and you made me a place
>now please keep the door open
>i would very much like to see who walks through next

>with love,
> ethereum

$xp 在3天前达到210万美金市值后，目前已经从高位下跌下跌到10万市值不到，跌幅超过95%。但在现在这个位置，非常有吸引力。

看似已经接近归零，但如果你去看stonks平台过去几天的项目，你会看到很多非常相似的k线走势

$allinu 在推出前3天下跌95%后，迅速从低位拉升到了3000万市值

$alice 在推出一周后下跌99%了，一周后从低位拉升到了130万市值

$gp 在推出第一周后下跌80%，一周后持续拉升，目前上涨到了1800万市值

为什么这些项目会在第一波看似死亡之后，第二波出现这么大的拉升幅度，核心还是取决于项目的质量以及第二波持有者的结构情况。

后面三种代币，用户买入后可以根据交易量获得源源不断的股票或着代币空投。 $xp 也是同理

在第一波被砸盘后，很快会有新的发现项目潜力的持有者加入，这些在二段底部果断抄底的新用户，通常持有周期更长，对stonks的理解更深。

在7-10万这个位置去买入 stonks 生态的“归零”项目，会有非常高的盈亏比和空投收益机会。

从7万到14万，涨幅1倍
从7万到50万，涨幅7倍
从7万到100万，涨幅14倍。
