text:
感谢币安广场邀请，前天在直播间聊了一个很多人都在讨论的话题。

AI 到底该继续踩油门，还是该踩刹车？

我的答案很简单，先踩刹车。

现在硅谷讲 AI，特别喜欢拍成《星际穿越》。一群天才科学家，为了全人类的未来，把自己锁在机房里燃烧生命。

实际情况可能更像《速度与激情》。

融资踩到底，GPU 买到冒烟，收入不够就循环投资，监管想跟上先排队三年。车里坐着 OpenAI、Meta、NVIDIA 和一堆基金，普通人也参与了，只不过位置比较特殊，我们在车底不是在车里。

直播里我主要讲了几个为什么现在必须开始谈减速的原因。

第一个是 Agent。

以前的大模型再聪明，大部分时候也只是嘴上厉害。现在完全不一样了。模型开始拿到浏览器、电脑、支付、代码仓库甚至公司内部系统的执行权。

AI 出问题的速度已经按月计算了，科技公司三个季度能把产品迭代三代，监管三个季度一般刚把第一次会开完。

第二个问题更现实，钱。

现在 AI 行业已经出现了一套非常魔幻的资金循环。

英伟达投 AI 公司，AI 公司拿钱买云，云厂商拿钱买英伟达 GPU。钱在产业链里转一圈，大家营收都很好看，唯一比较难判断的是需求到底有多少。

再配合服务器折旧年限不断拉长，利润表也开始拥有了一点 AI 特有的想象力。

服务器本身没有意见，审计师暂时也没有意见，最后有没有意见，可能要等泡沫破了以后才知道。

最麻烦的是，这场游戏的钱也早就不只是 VC 自己的钱。

养老金、指数基金、散户账户都已经被绑上来了。AI 股票涨的时候，大家一起庆祝新时代；哪天资本开支回报算不过来了，硅谷当然可以继续讲十年后的 AGI，退休的人可没那么多十年可以等。

这也是我最反感这轮 AI 狂热的一点。一小群人负责想象未来，几十亿人负责承担他们想错了的成本。

然后就是科技右翼。

Marc Andreessen 那套 techno-optimism 里，对监管、审慎和减速长期都抱着极大的敌意。硅谷现在很流行一种世界观，技术进步天然正确，只要未来足够宏大，今天付出一点代价都可以算「摩擦成本」。

问题来了，谁是摩擦？

一般不是 Marc Andreessen。

失业的人是摩擦，被算法淘汰的人是摩擦，被数据中心挤压电力资源的社区是摩擦，养老金跟着科技股一起坐过山车的人也是摩擦。

最后你会发现，每次谈为了全人类，真正需要牺牲一下的那批人，好像永远非常稳定。

所以我一直不太喜欢加速主义这套东西。

我不反对 AI，也不觉得技术应该停下来。医疗、科研、新药、教育，这些地方当然应该继续往前走。

但今天真正的问题是，谁决定往哪里加速，谁拿走收益，谁承担风险。

现在这三个问题的答案，都过于集中在少数科技公司和资本手里。

这种故事听多了，确实很容易产生信仰。

it's not custody and it's not fees. you can't launch an options venue with one contract, you need the whole board live at once, 500 to 1000 instruments across strikes and expiries. and the people selling the vol are institutions who won't move venues for a rebate. spreads on options are wide enough that incentives just don't work the way they do on perps.

text:
Replit co-founder and CEO Amjad Masad says many startups begin as premature optimization: founders raise money for ideas they don't care about.

"I think a lot of starting startups is premature optimization. I see it in a lot of kids now, where they're part of a group and a lot of their friends are raising a lot of money, and some of them are becoming unicorns."

"The motivation becomes envy, a really negative motivation as opposed to a positive one."

"They pre-commit to an idea they're not even interested in, raise money for it, and start pre-optimizing for some path that they haven't really reached yet. That's why I always come back to this idea of curiosity. What is actually driving you?"

"Once you find that idea that you want to dedicate your life to, or dedicate the next 10 years to, it's going to have such gravity that you're not going to be able to avoid it."

"I actively tried not to start Replit, but it exploded into a startup on its own. That's the feeling you should get: 'I guess I have to do it,' because there's so much momentum behind it."

"There's a predatory thing I've heard that happens right now where VCs go to Stanford students and give them a million dollars pre-idea... It's like the music industry... You're taking this young person and pre-committing them to something they shouldn't have committed to."

@amasad

text:
Any product that involves putting in money to get more money out in a short period of time is gambling.

There are many variations of this type of product and people will pretend it’s investing or truth seeking. But really it’s just selling entertainment in the form of gambling.

And the only way that type of entertainment works is when the win/lose ratio is razor thin.

Vegas historically has made trillions on a 1% edge.

But when a business comes along that is selling the same entertainment, but takes a 10, 20, 30% edge, and continues to pretend like it isn’t doing that, it’s really no surprise when customers revolt and take any change they can to demonize it.

Thanks for entertaining my vaguepost.

text:
I think it's time to hang up my Three.js hat.

Not because I'm quitting Three.js.

Because I no longer recognize the distinction between Three.js and physical reality.

First of all, this is not a pity post. I'll be fine. Probably. I'm also not 100% confident about any of this because my understanding of "outside" has deteriorated significantly over the past year.

But I'm an over-sharer and like to talk out loud, so I thought I would share some thoughts on where I see things going and why I'm considering stepping much, much further INTO Three.js development.

Some signals I've noticed lately:

-I'm the man.

-I rule

-Three.js rules

-Funkatron rules.

After thinking deeply about this, I've come to a completely different conclusion.

I need to go deeper.

Much deeper.

At this point, I don't want to USE Three.js.

I want to LIVE IN IT.

I want my house converted into a scene graph.

I want my kitchen to be scene.children[4].

I want to walk into my bathroom and have Chrome DevTools pop up because the toilet has a memory leak.

I want my wife to ask me where the car keys are and I want to say:

"Have you checked the object hierarchy?"

I want collision detection on the furniture.

I want my cats running on navmeshes.

I want my refrigerator to have an emissive map.

I want to physically walk into a room and hear:

renderer.render(scene, camera);

I no longer want windows.

I want viewports.

I no longer want lamps.

I want point lights.

I don't want a backyard.

I want a procedurally generated biome with LOD.

At some point I would also like to begin porting my consciousness into Java.

Yes, I know Three.js uses JavaScript.

That's exactly why nobody will see it coming.

I intend to migrate my soul one class at a time.

First the memories.

Then the personality.

Then whatever part of my brain keeps making me add fishing systems to everything.

Eventually my physical body will be deprecated.

My final biological act will be clicking:

npm install tc-poole

After that, I will exist exclusively inside a browser tab.

People will visit my site and occasionally hear a faint voice coming from the WebGL canvas saying:

"Try turning bloom up to 1.7."

I don't particularly care anymore whether I personally typed every line of code.

I care whether the spaceship flies.

People say AI has taken away the challenge.

Meanwhile I am now simultaneously a game developer, systems architect, animator, webmaster, shader technician, database administrator, level designer, lore historian, sound engineer, UI designer, network engineer, digital cartographer, fake meteorologist, imaginary economist, and municipal planner for cities that do not exist.

Yesterday I spent an hour trying to determine whether a fictional moon should increase the drop rate of a fictional fish.

I have never been more intellectually occupied.

So yes.

I think it's time to step away from Three.js.

Approximately thirty feet away.

Then sprint directly toward it at full speed.

I'm not leaving Three.js.

I'm attempting to achieve Three.js escape velocity.

The long-term plan is simple:

Phase 1: Build websites with Three.js.

Phase 2: Build games with Three.js.

Phase 3: Build worlds with Three.js.

Phase 4: Move into the worlds.

Phase 5: Transfer consciousness into Java.

Phase 6: Realize I should have used JavaScript.

Phase 7: Become an undocumented browser feature.

Phase 8: Achieve immortality as a console warning.

So no, this is not my retirement announcement.

This is my announcement that I am abandoning conventional reality.

I'm not stepping away from Three.js.

I'm stepping further INTO Three.js.

If anybody needs me, I'll be somewhere around scene.position.z = -4000.

God help us all.

第一步，发一个币股 Meme，交易税直接拉到 3%。

找 FOMO 上的 KOL、交易员、X 上的喊单账号，把这个币推到所有人面前。

先控筹码 → 再拿手续费分成 → KOL 制造注意力 → 散户进场交易 → 继续产生手续费 → 热度起来后，再慢慢把早期筹码卖出去。

第一遍赚的是交易税。

第二遍赚的是早期筹码退出。

这是真正的“永赚宝典”。

text:
2年前，正值比特币L2 文艺复兴，细分赛道出现了百链大战的盛况；

2年后，这批BTC L2 机构链几近消亡，一轮周期下来牌桌上的龙头还是Stacks。

@Stacks 作为最老牌的BTC 侧链/ L2，主网已经平稳运行了近6年时间。Stacks 链的龙头生态位，则被 @ZestProtocol 长期霸占。

据Defillama 数据，Zest 协议存款峰值达到 $100M+，目前协议TVL 7473万美元，占Stacks 全链TVL 的比重高达84.7%。

Zest 的主营业务是借贷，几乎垄断了Stacks 链上的借贷市场。值得关注的是，Zest 正将协议重定位成比特币资本层，开始将触角伸向下游衍生业务，做BTC 抵押金库，将闲置的BTC 变成生产性资产吃收益。

抵押生息金库的技术实现逻辑比较符合bitcoin OG 的胃口：BTC 无需wrap、无需进资金池、无需托管，是一种带约束的自托管机制。

可以简单理解成：用户先把BTC 打进Bitcoin L1 的一个Taproot UTXO 金库，并通过预签名将花费路径锁死；目标链（如以太坊）上生成抵押证明vaultBTC；拿这张抵押证明去抵押借款，结清贷款后时间锁到期无条件取回。

Zest 官方近期一直把Bitcoin Collateral Vaults 作为第一优先级，昨天终于上线主网Demo 版，但目前有存款额度限制(单个钱包最多存0.001 BTC)。产品铺开后Zest 的TVL 大概率要再上一个台阶。

看了眼Zest 的原生代币市值并不高，2600万美元流通市值，上了bn alpha 和合约。可以把Stacks 和Zest 先加入关注列表，等比特币生态赛道的风来。

text:
Starknet might be one of the most interesting places for memes.

 Why?

• Cheap gas, so small trades don't get eaten by fees
• STRK20 lets you swap privately while using public liquidity
• @StarkLaunchy makes launching a meme coin simple
• @BrotherUnrug adds liquidity locks and anti-bot protections
@EkuboProtocol + @avnu_fi handle the trading
• Ethereum security + StarkWare ZK tech

But the big one for me is privacy.

On most meme chains, your wallet is fully public.

People can see what you bought, how much you bought, when you entered, when you sold and what you're holding.

This makes it easy for snipers and copy traders to follow your moves.

With STRK20, you can use protected balances and private swaps while still trading with public liquidity.

So you can buy a meme without immediately showing everyone your position.

You can also take profits without making your whole trading history public.

Basically, the market stays public, but your wallet activity doesn't have to.

Solana still has the biggest meme volume, and Base has Coinbase behind it.

But Starknet is building something different: cheap launches, cheap trading, privacy when you want it, and strong infrastructure.

The meme scene on Starknet is still early.

Stay locked in.

ethereum:0xa12cc123ba206d4031d1c7f6223d1c2ec249f4f3 的隐私是全同态加密 (FHE)
把数据，余额，仓位全部都加密起来。

普通的加密技术只可以在储存的部分保密，如果要进行计算，得把数据都解密。

谁说鱼和熊掌不可兼得？

ethereum:0xa12cc123ba206d4031d1c7f6223d1c2ec249f4f3 还可以选择性授权，
例如需要合规的时候，把权限交给指定的对象，
监管和机构的隐私都兼顾了。
不过 FHE 现在计算成本可不算便宜，速度也较慢。

所以隐私也有很多方向，

ethereum:0xa12cc123ba206d4031d1c7f6223d1c2ec249f4f3 是技术牛逼，对未来的想象力比较大，不过它还得克服速度和成本。

author: 0xOmnia
quoted_text:
Every crypto founder thinks they need to time their token launch around bull markets. I always tell them they're wrong, launch timing doesn't matter. They never believe me.

Well, I built a tool with Claude Code to analyze every token listing announced on the Binance blog to settle this once and for all. 

Here's what I found:
Headline result: there is no statistically significant difference between tokens launched in bull vs bear markets (Mann-Whitney p = 0.81), meaning differences between bull and bear market tokens are indistinguishable from noise.

It doesn't matter when you launch your token.

How can I be sure of that?

First, you have to be careful how you answer this question: people believe that it's better to launch tokens in bull markets, and there's more funding in bull markets, so there are many more tokens launched in bull markets. Because of this sample bias, you can't naively look at the proportion of top 100 tokens that were launched in bull markets.
To correct for this, you need a clean selection criterion to compare the populations. The best dataset I found was looking at the Binance listings blog. Take every announced listing, tag them as during bull markets, bear markets, or neutral markets, and benchmark the relative performance of the bull vs bear populations. Filter out tokens that aren't independently priced (RWAs, stablecoins, LSTs etc.), and this gets you a total of ~200 tokens to benchmark.

See the website below to explore the data & methodology in more detail. This finding is robust to almost any way you slice and dice the data.

Now, if you're a founder, this analysis might not be the end of the story. Even if launching in a bear market doesn't predict long-term token performance, there are other advantages to launching in a bear market: less competition for talent, service providers are cheaper, exchange listings are less competitive. On the flipside, if you're doing a simultaneous token sale, you're likely to get more demand in a bull market.

But on the whole, these things are probably a wash. The main thing is to just get your product out there and build something valuable.

The example I always bring up to founders is that Solana launched 4 days after the COVID crash in 2020, when Bitcoin wicked down to $4K.

It doesn't matter that much when you launch. Just launch.

We've all been there. Someone you trust says "just buy it", and you either go all in on vibes or spend hours reading earnings reports you don't fully understand.

So I tried something different. I asked Minara, an AI built only for investing, to do the homework a Wall Street analyst would do:

→ Gave me the bull case AND the bear case
→ Listed 3 things that would prove each side wrong

That last part is what changed how I think about it. Instead of asking "should I buy?", you start asking "what would make me change my mind?"

Then I opened its sources to check the numbers myself. Don't blindly trust your friend, and don't blindly trust an AI either.

text:
So excited to introduce Muse Realtime Avatars which brings any character into a live conversation! This is a big milestone on a journey that started two years ago at Waveforms, and I’m so proud of what we’ve built. Since moving over to MSL, we've been rebuilding the realtime AI inference stack at Meta to enable both realtime voice and video conversations at scale.

From a technology POV, realtime multimodal inference is probably one of the most interesting and complex problems in AI Infra. It touches every part of the stack from model and hardware optimizations to LLM orchestration and the RTC stack. Every millisecond matters. Especially at scale. Realtime voice inference is cool, but compute-bound diffusion-based video models add a whole new dimension and bring an entirely new set of challenges. Our work makes it possible to serve these models at low latency and cost-effectively at Meta’s scale.

From an experience perspective, I find these interactions magical. Personal superintelligence can’t be truly personal unless you can express yourself in modalities beyond text. And so I’m super excited that Muse Realtime Avatars are coming to Muse! We'll have more to share soon, but for now check out this blogpost about our work :)

* 比特币极端主义者的谢林点（Schelling Point）极度坚固，明面上“只有 BTC，别无他物”。但在私下，他们也是人，无法免疫贪婪与避险本能。正如 2021 年 Su Zhu 提到的“比特币人偷偷跑冷钱包买 ETH”一样，今天大量比特币人开始将 ZEC 作为隐私与量子威胁的对冲。
* 数学逻辑：1.7 万亿的庞然大物，只需要 1% 的 BTC 财富为了“以防万一”换仓买入 ZEC，对一个中型市值资产来说就是近乎无限的溢价拉升。驱动 ZEC 的不是美元，是 BTC 的财富本身。

2️⃣ NEAR 的逻辑：赢得“智能合约换仓”奖杯

* 同样的故事正在 NEAR 身上发生。NEAR 赢下了 2026 年的“智能合约换仓”奖杯。
* 买盘来源：对传统蓝筹（ETH/SOL）脱节的技术债感到厌倦的资金。
* 随着 ETH/SOL 等老牌蓝筹技术债堆积、回报率边际递减，市场不再愿意为旧叙事买单。NEAR 凭借新一代技术架构吸引了这部分散落但极其庞大的智能合约流转资金。

3️⃣ 行业暗面：“蓝筹诅咒”与价值捕获的断层

* 老大老二涨不动了：BTC 尚未完全演变成黄金替代品，ETH 也缺乏支撑 10 倍重估的新叙事。
* 价值被 Web2 捕获：Hyperliquid、Venice、Morpho 等创新不断涌现，但如果加密总市值无法突破 10 万亿，这些新秀创造的价值，很大程度上不会回馈给 BTC/ETH，反而会被 Robinhood、Coinbase、Apollo 等传统券商和机构捕获。

山寨爆发的本质是谢林点的转移。只要你能说服 1.7 万亿 BTC 资产里的极小一部分“买一点以防万一”，就能缔造下一个千亿神话。

🪂来看看 32% 比例的空投方案明确了什么？

先说市场最关心的空投。

Variational @variational_io  并首次给出了较完整的代币分配方案：

🔹32% 为创始分配，即按用户持有的 Variational 积分比例空投，TGE 时全部解锁；
🔹18% 进入生态储备，由 Variational Foundation 用于生态发展；
🔹50% 分配给团队和投资者，TGE 后锁定 12 个月，此后用至少 3 年时间解锁；团队与投资者各自所占比例将在 TGE 前公布。

这也解释了此前官方文档中「约 50% 代币将分配给社区」的表述：32% 创世空投加上 18% 生态储备，合计正好为 50%。

空投的基本计算逻辑可以写成：

个人获得的 VAR 数量= 个人积分 ÷ 最终有效积分总量 × 代币总量的 32%

官方同时规定，账户至少需要持有 1 个积分，并签署相应服务条款，才有资格领取；未被领取的创世分配代币将被销毁。

每周仍将发放 15 万积分，持续到 TGE。这意味着，如果用户的积分不再增加，而全网积分继续增长，其在 32% 空投池中的占比就会下降。

此前 Entropy Advisors 制作的 Dune 空投模拟器假设积分活动在第三季度结束、最终积分总量为 915 万，并模拟了不同 FDV 与空投比例下的积分价值。若 FDV 达到 10 亿美元，单个积分价格达到 37.84 美元。

现在 32% 的比例已经确定，但积分活动被延长至 TGE，因此 915 万不能再直接视为最终分母。模拟器中的「每积分价格」和「预计空投价值」仍只是情景测算，不是官方估值或兑付承诺。

Entropy Advisors 制作的另外一个仪表板显示，Variational 平台总地址数量有 18.95 万个，其中活跃地址数量有 12.33 万个。

代币价值捕获方面，Variational 最新公告称，计划将「进入协议金库的收入」全部用于回购并销毁 $VAR。需要注意，这并不等于 Omni 的全部收入都会回购代币。

目前官方文档显示，协议金库暂时获得 OLP（Omni Liquidity Provider）价差收入的 20%，且这一比例仍可能调整；具体回购频率、执行方式和代币用途也要等 TGE 前进一步披露。

quoted_text:
Two weeks ago I had two "gold" tokens open in CoinMarketCap's RWA API, priced 30x apart.

Spent a good while convinced I'd found free money. I hadn't. 

One was priced per gram, the other per troy ounce. Nothing in the API says that anywhere.

So I stopped building a screener.

If I can get that wrong looking at raw data, someone scanning wrapper prices on a DEX has no shot.

Bedrock ranks live spreads between an asset's wrappers, tells you who issued each one and what chain it's on, and links the SEC filings. 

Mostly so when a spread looks too good you can find out whether it's real or just a unit mismatch.

All off CoinMarketCap's RWA API.

cybersecurity is essentially an economics and game theory problem. the role of the defender is to strategically allocate budget to minimize risk. think of this allocation as insurance, it does not generate a "Return On Investment" as it would if the same budget were to be allocated to the Sales, Go To Market or other department that brings in revenue. this is the first step to understand why security teams are often times underfunded and overworked.

when you first create a cybersecurity department the organization has a massive attack surface, the first units of investment yield massive risk reductions, for example: implementing MFA, buying modern EDRs, inventory and discovering assets, etc.. the ROSI (Return On Security Investment) is high because the financial damage prevented by stopping a highly likely breach far outweighs the cost of the security tools.

after certain point, when the highest probability hacks are "insured", spending more on security does not buy you more security.

running an offensive operation was limited by time, skill and resources. AI has completely changed the attacker economics. anyone can use an agent to hack anything they want. it's that bad, and it's that easy. the constraints are not skill and time anymore, only compute, which keeps getting cheaper (inference cost, speed and intelligence per dollar). attackers can afford testing hundreds of angles simultaneously like combining phishing, supply chain attacks and API vulnerabilities.

as attacker capabilities improve and become cheaper, defender effectiveness decline per unit of investment. defenders need to invest across the entire expanding attack surface which dilutes the effectiveness of every dollar spent. and since cybersecurity is not a revenue driver, there isn't much incentive from executives to invest in something they cannot measure the return on.

cybersecurity is a dynamic, asymmetric, multi-stage game against an adaptive adversary with a default structural advantage who is increasingly transforming into an autonomous machine. you cannot fight this with a traditional investment model.

text:
Wanted to run a proper tweet where I cover many questions regarding LONG. Bookmark this, it’s going to be quite in depth.

Before I start, I want to clarify that this is an educational effort. One of our core values with LONG is not to look down on our users but actually equip them with the right knowledge and prove another type of playbook can exist in the space.

There is no reason for us to be defensive(esp not on tech) LONG proves itself every day and we will keep doing so. I also think there is a fine line between slightly disingenuous FUD vs critical thinking, so pay attention to it as well.

#1 Why is LONG optimizing for liquidity as the moat with stock pairs and generally?

Main problem in the space = not lack of motion but lack of stability (that drives rotation and lack of conviction)

Deep liquidity solves two things: bundling and supply control are very expensive + the market can absorb extreme periods of volatility.

Deep stock liquidity creates a black hole or a magnet where a LONG pair effectively becomes a secondary market for the tokenized stock and keeps a high % of circ (demonstrated in many pairs)

This is the biggest pure “DeFi” flywheel and is similar to how network effects evolve around lending protocols, DEXs like Uniswap and so on. Stock liquidity is a moat that enables users to become “market makers” and share the upside of any downstream effect coming from it (increased trading activity on the stock itself, any new utilities like lending, and simply being a source for arb)

#2 How exactly are stock pairs correlated with their underlying stocks?

DEX pairs have a sell side and a buy side. With stock pairs, the buy side is the new token and the sell side is the tokenized stock. When the stock goes up, the USD value of stock liquidity goes along with it. This is exactly how majors were able to bootstrap the trenches in the early days of Sol + ETH. The major or stock going up = the Fed printing new money supply or giving stimulus.

In practice:

- If the stock went up by 20%, there is now 1.2x more stock liquidity in the pool, so selling the same token amount will give 1.2x more in USD value(rule of thumb)

- This also means the impact on the chart is becoming smoother

- What makes it more impactful is the depth of liquidity. If it’s 10k worth of total stock liquidity, it wouldn't matter because a 5k trade will drain the pool completely

-LONG pairs are not just super liquid generally, they are also ranked as the largest sources of stock liq for the tokenized stock pools(AI is the 2nd largest source of NVDA on RH)

#3 Two sides of the same coin: How do arbitrage and price coupling actually play out onchain when the stock price rises?

Something VERY important to keep in mind. AI priced in NVDA and NVDA priced in AI are two sides of the same coin. You can’t have a significant depeg between the implied price of NVDA in AI vs NVDA in USDG, and the same applies to AI in NVDA vs AI in USDG.

Take the following scenario: NVDA just went up by 5%, the oracle updates immediately, and now there are 2 sec for the new NVDA price to update onchain. An arb race starts:

1. Arb starts with buying AI on the AI/USDG pool (front-running on a stale NVDA price)

2. AI is being sold on the AI/NVDA pool, receiving NVDA

3. The arb bot now holds X NVDA they bought at a discount

4. The arb profit depends on how fast they can sell it on the updated NVDA/USDG pool + an optimized sell size

This is a bit of a simplistic flow because, in effect, this is happening 24/7 and AI/NVDA is effectively a coordination mech to keep prices in sync.

The more NVDA liq there is on the AI/NVDA pool, the more predictable this arb can be and the more “utility” builds into AI/NVDA just by being a large source of liq. This is not simple reflexivity but more of a compounding long-term game.

Exactly the same effect takes place when NVDA dumps, but in this case it’s actually helping the AI (USD price) absorb volatility in a much smoother way (happened a few weeks ago when NVDA had the 1st 7d down streak since ‘22 and AI actually went up)

one can think about what might happen when we drop the assumption that the price of onchain NVDA or any stock follows the stock market, and the price of onchain NVDA is actually driving the arb offchain (I’ll leave it as an exercise for the readers)

#4 The LONG term game is dist >> fee capture/dividend

The only way for an asset like AI to go up is having consistent flows of net new marginal buyers that are willing to buy at a higher price. This is typical growth. Every single incentive we can place on top of it gets stronger when the asset becomes bigger.

A good way to think about it is stock dividends. An early-stage stock that starts handing out dividends over reinvesting into higher growth is simply sacrificing these gains.

Having an asset like AI at 1b would be correlated with the ability to capture more value back to holders, whether through “dividends”, voting rights or NVDA accumulation. It won’t necessarily be a 50% APY but more similar to 1-3%, with real size (NVDA did 6b in dividends last quarter and it was just $0.25 per share)

#5 Why do AI pools with USDG and ETH have so much vol and is it good?

Part of it goes back to my prev point regarding arb, the other part is also all sorts of AI pairs.

Having an AI/AI-pair makes it cheaper to go from USDG→AI→pair vs USDG→NVDA→AI→pair.

A few immediate positive effects:

1. We already internalize this effect with AI pairs as fees remove more AI from circ regardless of whether it was routed via the main AI/NVDA pool. It also locks more AI in uncorrelated pools

2. More vol = more fees to external LPs = higher incentive to provide more liq to back AI on any pool

There is no perfect fee/hook that can fully eliminate it (and it might be undesirable) for two reasons:

1. If we were to relaunch AI with 0.15%, anyone can still set up a pool with a 0.1% fee. These undercuts are very common and it’s a race to the bottom type of situation

2. You need extremely centralized and active LP management. I don’t think anyone would have wanted LONG or any launcher to have the option to just rug the entire LP

#6 Is it possible to 10x NVDA accumulation or have more fee and vol capture ?

Yes! Take, for example, some of our more active LP actions: we’ve added 200k worth of NVDA as a sell wall on the AI/NVDA pool. Yesterday we did something similar with 200k worth of LongX assets. Adding these into the community vault, for example, would have increased the total NVDA worth by 2x.

There are dozens of other ways to do it with more sophisticated mechs. And it reminds me of the early days of the vault when users asked why we didn’t just use a buyback vault instead.

This goes back to my prev point: the potential of monetization via fees is capped by the size of the asset. Anything we can do today to grow AI will pay 10x more in the future when we would want to start rolling it out.

#7 “If you don’t know where the yield is coming from, you are the yield” Why is LONG not supporting reflections out of the box?

Note that all of the prev points about how easy it is to undercut high-tax pools, how liquidity capture is the moat, and how organic non-incentivized growth is the real key apply even more strongly to the typical reflection mech.

We think the sort of DeFi summer APY maxxing is a not part of our vision of stock pairs. We want users to buy early and hold, not because they can farm fees (which can be done on any yield-style protocol even a stable pair)

We want them to buy and hold because they want to align with the stock and grow a movement around it.

Generally:

High-yield products in crypto have ended up dying

The PMF for yield is actually super solid yield (the biggest vault on RH is USDG with 3% APY)

I think this is a bit like creator fees. Incentivized vol over sustainability, and it’s so damn easy to just buy 20% at low FDV and have a no-lose option forever, then dump to move to the next as vol decays. 

Hope you were able to go through it! :) 

LONG.

text:
BlackRock argues AI agents are an underappreciated source of demand for stablecoins and crypto rails. I checked what agents actually pay on-chain today.

The answer is very little. After removing activity flagged as wash trading, x402 runs at roughly $3 - 7M a year. 

BlackRock benchmarks agentic payments against $11T in annual stablecoin volume. That is a gap of about six orders of magnitude.

Most of the public x402 numbers were never real. Two-thirds of all volume since October 2025 is flagged as gamed. The November peak everyone cited was $28.6M in raw volume and $5.1M after filtering.

What is left is concentrated. One server, sol_blockrun_ai, took 81% of top-100 x402 volume over the last 30 days. It is a pay-per-request LLM gateway: 68 buyers, 21.7M transactions, $0.013 per call.

That is the interesting part. The only x402 use case with real money is agents paying for inference, which is exactly BlackRock's compute thesis. The direction is right. The market is not there yet. 

An on-chain OpenRouter-style gateway processed about $290K last month. Stripe reportedly agreed to pay $7B+ for the off-chain one.

Meta 这次真把 AI 做成电子宠物了。

Meta Connect 上，扎克伯格掏出了一块巴掌大的 Muse Charm，专门用来跟 Muse Agent 说话。大概两英寸 OLED 屏，内置 5G，还有前后摄像头、指纹传感器，挂钥匙上就能带着走。点一下，不用掏手机、不用开 App，直接把 Muse 喊出来干活。Meta 计划 12 月开卖，价格还没公布。

text:
USDv is live.

This is the culmination of more than two years of work. Weirdly enough, the time it took brought us back to our original thesis: a dollar that earns.

One token. No staking, no wrapping, no vaults. A dollar you can keep using while it earns.

We changed a lot along the way. What became absolutely clear was how much needed to exist underneath that simple idea to make it work at scale.

Onchain dollars are already productive...just not for you. 

The income rarely reaches you or the apps using them. We built the infrastructure to change that, allowing the dollar and its income to move separately. Your dollar goes where you need it, while the income can still reach you.

The dollar sits underneath so much of what happens onchain. Teams raise in it, treasuries hold it, markets trade against it. Those dollars should be able to earn while continuing to do all of those things. A dollar providing liquidity is already doing useful work. It should also deliver the income from its backing.

That’s the improvement we’ve spent two years working toward. Preserving the dollar’s composability means its productivity can extend into the places where people actually use it.

Building this also showed us how the same infrastructure could apply to other assets with economics to distribute. There’s a much broader thesis there that I’ll share more about.

For now, USDv is live, our first partners are adopting it, and the work ahead is making it useful everywhere you’d want to use a dollar.

Thank you to our team, our community, and everyone who believed in this early enough to help us get here.

I hope what feels like an upgrade today eventually feels obvious.

In 1999, Anna Bagelholm was skiing in Sweden when she accidentally fell into a frozen river. She was stuck in the ice for over 80 minutes as rescuers struggled to free her. When they finally pulled her from the freezing cold water she was given CPR, and she was defibrillated, but the rescue team were sure she was dead.

It took two hours to get her to the hospital, by which point her body temperature was 56 degrees Fahrenheit. At the hospital she was connected to an EKG, which showed no signs of life, so doctors declared her clinically dead.

The doctors didn’t want to give up on her, so more than 100 medical staff worked in 9-hour shifts to try and revive her. Miraculously, they were able to warm up her blood and achieve a heartbeat. They then put her on a ventilator for the next 35 days.

Anna eventually woke from the coma but was paralysed from the neck down. She was angry with her friends at first for saving her life, but somehow managed to make a full recovery and now works as a radiologist.

text:
so... $CRCL or ripple:native ? 

Circle (USDC) and Ripple (RLUSD) are stablecoin competitors >>> both just wrote checks into the SAME coin-agnostic settlement startup, alongside Visa Ventures. @Finextra: Velocity's Series A extension +$10M -> ~$48M at a $200M mark. Why fund the layer that abstracts your own coin away?

> Velocity (London, founded May-2025; founder Tom Greenwood, ex-Volt/IFX Payments) sells coin-agnostic orchestration — banking rails + compliance + custody + settlement so incumbents bolt on stablecoins without ripping out existing stacks

> backers: Visa Ventures (NEW), Circle Ventures, Ripple — a USDC issuer and an RLUSD issuer on the same cap table

> local: no US Form D — the $10M and all three strategics' stakes are EDGAR-invisible (UK-private); litigation null on Velocity + Greenwood + Queathem; sanctions clean

> local: immaterial to backers' P&L — V (~$730B) barely moved; CRCL -7% Sep15 then -11% on Arc-launch day, coin-commoditization tape, not this check

> pattern: Circle bought Tazapay (09-09), MA owns BVNK ($1.8B), Visa's in Zero Hash — they keep buying the abstraction layer, not the coin

> likely >> Circle funding a coin-agnostic orchestrator is a defensive hedge: if settlement is abstracted behind banks' existing rails, nobody cares which coin clears -> USDC/RLUSD lose pricing power (Circle rev +7% vs volume +150% already shows the coin decoupling from usage). A seat inside the thing that commoditizes your coin beats disintermediation.

> next >> by CRCL Q3 (~mid-Nov)/V FY-Q4 (late-Oct): Velocity stays coin-agnostic, NO default coin named, AND a strategic deepens to commercial/M&A (Circle->Tazapay template) OR a rival takes a competing-orchestrator stake; AND CRCL's USDC dollar-share stays flat-to-down. Velocity naming USDC or RLUSD as default settlement = one issuer captured the layer, read wrong.

>>> since it's alt season ripple:native for me pls

text:
Sam Altman 职业生涯里回报最高的一年，是那一年他手里没工作，到处探索自己感兴趣的东西，还遇到了一堆愿意教他的人

“我卖掉自己那家公司的时候大概26岁，差不多就是那个年纪

之后我在收购我的那家公司待了一小段时间，可能是25岁，记不太清了

再往后我干脆空了一整年，什么正经工作都没做

我特别推荐你们也这么干
回过头看，那一年可能是我整个职业生涯里最好的两三件事之一

那一年里，我读了几十本教科书
我把以前一直感兴趣、但一直没时间去碰的那些方向都摸了一遍

我当时完全没想到，这些东西后来会以那种方式串到一起

我学了很多核工程的东西
那时候AI刚开始有点苗头，所以我学了很多AI

我还学了合成生物学
还学了投资

也就是从那一年开始，我对投资这件事认真起来了

在这之前我大概投过四五个天使，都是随手投的，也没当回事

那一年我算是下决心了，我说行，我要认真试试这件事，看看自己是不是真的喜欢

我到处跑，去了很多地方
慢慢对世界其他地方到底长什么样有了感觉，比之前的感受多得多

我遇到各种人在做各种不同的事情，他们都愿意跟我聊，愿意花时间跟我讲
我还拿到了一直缺的那段时间，重新把朋友和家人接上

就是把生活整个理顺了一遍

然后我就去帮那些看起来值得帮的人，反正我那时候最不缺的就是时间

所以如果我碰到一个有意思的人，看起来还不错又需要帮忙，我就直接去帮
他们会教我点东西，或者以后给我一个投他们公司的机会

我特意不给自己排日程，这样随时可以拎包就走，飞去另一个国家参加个会

我就开始做各种乱七八糟的事
现在回头看，这些事几乎全都没成
但种子是埋下去了，后来有些东西是真真正正长出来的，而且是长在很深的地方”

text:
在做了6个月产品
功能臃肿后，我觉得做产品很难
真的很难

最难的不在于我想做什么，最难的是把某个行为的内核解刨出来，然后去思考我们怎么把这件事用一个可视以及便利的ui去做展示。同时也要思考用户心理和模拟揣测用户使用

我手上有很多feature在backlog里，不是不想做。而是完全没有想清楚应该怎么去呈现这个ui和交互。这里再提一个概念，想法和思维的抽象通过不同组件形成一个可解释的形态。不亚于把哲学或是deep tech解释成凡俗语言

最后就是举个例子，最近想做的一个改动。叙事中有两种不同的时间线。时序和单一事件，时序就是故事发展的时间顺序，单一事件就很好了解。可是，问题来单一事件是时效性的，但是单一事件又能是非线性的。例如伏笔和事件关联，还有因果关系。我们现在做了一版是基于章节的。我觉得不行。但是这个复杂的关系网络要层层拆解又很难，所以就暂且搁置了。最近看哲学有感又从backlog拉出来，看看怎么实现
author: timtimtim_eth
quoted_text:
efficiency, productivity, speed

we keep worshipping these words like they are what we live for

ship faster
merge more
manage more agents
compress every loop
remove every pause
turn every hour into output

but what is the point of endless production if there is no time left to think deeply?

not react
not optimize
not summarize
not clear the queue

think

to sit with a question long enough that your real intention starts to appear  
to find the purpose underneath the motion  
to ask whether the thing being accelerated should exist at all

ai could be a new canvas

a way to make strange things
personal things
impossible things
tools, worlds, poems, games, interfaces, films, languages, rituals
things that let more people touch the shape of their own imagination

but instead, so much of it is becoming slop factories

more content
more funnels
more tickets
more fake work pretending to be value

you can merge 2000 prs
you can manage 500 agents
you can wake up to dashboards proving that the machine kept moving while you slept

but what is the point if you only sleep 5 hours a day?

what is the point if you stop talking to other humans?
stop learning about the past?
stop playing?
stop wandering?
stop being surprised?

what is the point if your whole life becomes optimizing the system that is consuming you?

speed is not meaning
scale is not wisdom
automation is not freedom if it only makes everyone run faster

and where are we running?

toward what?

a world where every person becomes a manager of machines, and every machine produces more things no one had the time to truly want?

the danger is not that ai makes us lazy

the danger is that ai makes us endlessly busy

that it gives us infinite production before we have found intention
infinite execution before we have developed taste
infinite motion before we have learned how to be still

maybe the real frontier is not more speed

maybe it is discernment

knowing what not to make
knowing when to stop
knowing when the most productive thing is to sleep, read history, call a friend, play with a cat, walk without tracking it, or stare at the ceiling until the false urgency dissolves

tools should give us more life
not turn life into a tool

if ai is going to matter, it should not just help us produce more

it should help us become more human  
more imaginative
more free

otherwise, it’s the same old factory
just without humans

教大家在新加坡海南咖啡店点单的小技巧
kopi 就是带奶+糖的咖啡 （这里的奶=炼乳）
kopi o 就是不带奶 带糖 
kopi o kosong 就是咖啡，不带糖不带奶

beng/ice 就是冰

所以如果你要带走一杯冰美式 alike的传统海南冰咖啡就是 kopi - o - kosong - beng dabao 

另，建议如果你有时间，可以去亚坤的店里喝杯热的kopi，感受传统的海南风味细节

这个细节就是温杯

师傅在泡的时候会先把热水倒在咖啡杯里，然后依据当时候店里的人数决定热水在杯里停留多久再倒掉，再把咖啡液倒在里头

服务员把送到你的桌子再到你的手碰到咖啡杯的柄就正好是35-40度左右…
海南咖啡的温度

这是你在星巴克感受不到的细节
author: agintender
quoted_text:
新加坡见，不止在会场。

前两天和朋友翻旧推，翻到第一次去新加坡时写的那句：

“你好，这是我看 F1 的第一次，是你的第几次？”

一转眼，今年已经是第三年参加 TOKEN2049 了

从第一次什么都不懂，到现在能带着朋友跑会，梅西也算攒了点经验😂

于是把近几年的跑会TIPS放在这里！给今年来新加坡、尤其是第一次来的朋友，少走一点弯路👇

1️⃣ 先把几天的重要安排记住

▪️10 月 6 日：OKX Now
▪️10 月 7–8 日：TOKEN2049 主会，滨海湾金沙
▪️10 月 9–11 日：F1 新加坡站

这几天都按新加坡当地时间，和北京、香港没有时差

主会门票、Side Event 报名、OKX Now 邀请、F1 门票，不能通用。申请提交，不等于审核通过，出发前记得检查确认邮件

2️⃣ OKX Now

10 月 6 日，从上午的产品发布和现场演示，到下午的行业对话

期待和大家面对面聊聊，也想听听你们看完产品后的真实反馈💚

提醒一下：OKX Now 是邀请制，只有获确认的嘉宾才能参加。收到海报或提交申请，不等于已经完成入场确认

受邀的朋友，提前和邀请人核对好时间、地址及签到方式

酒店名字也要看清：Pan Pacific Orchard，不是 Pan Pacific Singapore

别跑错了😂 具体入场信息以确认邀请为准

⚠️活动有地区适用限制，详见官方活动说明 https://t.co/qY1ybeK9T6。不能到现场的朋友，也欢迎关注官方直播～

3️⃣ 去看 F1，听我一句劝：尽量坐地铁！

比赛期间周边封路、绕行，坐 MRT 通常更省心。先看门票对应的入场口，再选下车站，不是所有人都去同一个站

而且相关封路安排从 10 月 7 日就开始了，主会期间也会影响部分滨海湾周边交通

💡地铁支付提前准备好：

▫️带非接触支付标志、符合要求的 Visa／Mastercard，可以直接刷

▫️或者买 EZ-Link 交通卡

▫️微信、支付宝付款码不能直接当作这里的地铁乘车码

▫️进出站用同一张卡或同一台手机，别进去刷手机、出来换实体卡

去 TOKEN2049 主会场，地铁认准 Bayfront 站，不是 Marina Bay 站；

打车直接搜 Sands Expo & Convention Centre，不要只填「金沙酒店」

4️⃣ Side Event 不用报满，先想清楚自己想见谁

找活动可以收藏这张 @punk2898  做的中文地图：https://t.co/0isEbrvjoV

先定当天最想去的一两场，再找附近顺路的活动。地图帮你找线索，最终时间、费用、地址和入场要求，还是看主办方原页面

也不用把社交全部安排在晚上。晨跑、早餐会、咖啡局、Workshop，都可以认识人。

5️⃣ 住哪里

▫️乌节路附近活动多：优先看 Orchard 一带。
▫️主会安排满：优先考虑去金沙方便的位置。
▫️想兼顾预算和交通：可以看看 Bugis、Bencoolen、Chinatown，具体看酒店离地铁多远。

订房之前可以多看一眼含税总价、取消政策、有没有窗、是不是独立卫浴，以及到地铁实际要走多远。房费省下来的钱，别最后都花在打车上😂

退房当天还要继续跑会的话，提前问好酒店能不能寄存行李，给取行李和去机场留够时间

6️⃣ 吃饭可以简单，约饭尽量提前

想吃本地餐食、控制预算，可以把 Maxwell、牛车水大厦熟食中心、老巴刹放进备选。早餐找顺路的亚坤，正餐也可以考虑松发

想吃辣椒蟹，就提前订位、问清重量和价格，不要夹在两场会议之间赶着吃

餐厅标价后面如果有“++”，记得看服务费和税。比如收取 10% 服务费和 9% GST 时，标价 S$100，最后是 S$119.90

熟食中心吃完记得收好托盘、餐具和桌面垃圾

7️⃣ 最后：出发前检查清单

□ SG Arrival Card：抵达前的三天内提交，包含抵达当天。ICA 官方渠道免费，免签不等于不用填

□ 手机卡：有流量不一定能打电话、收短信，原手机号记得保留接验证码的能力

□ 支付：可用的银行卡＋少量新币现金，留个备用 

□ 随身带：薄外套、雨具、充电宝、好走路的鞋 

□ 入场凭证：提前存好，晒图记得打码 

□ 约见地址：写清哪家酒店、哪一层、哪个入口

如果晚上正好在金沙附近，也可以留点时间看水舞秀，或者去滨海湾花园看灯光。但是需要留意当天开放和交通安排嗷！

前两次 TOKEN 留下的回忆都太特别，希望这一次，见到想见的人，留下的都是开心

10 月，大家，新加坡见！

text:
once i'm in a spot position i'm comfortable holding long term, i try to stop looking at the chart. maybe a glance at the 3d or weekly every so often, daily even less. i did my research, picked my level, bought it. after that the chart mostly just gives me reasons to get in my own head.

when things start trending, ta gets pretty useless for long stretches, and it was already fuzzy to begin with. if i stare at it long enough i'll find something bearish and let it mess with how i'm thinking about the position.

what i actually care about is where we are in the cycle overall, where btc is vs where i think it can go, how long i've been holding, and how the rest of the market and sentiment look. most of that i get from being on here and talking to people.

i did not follow any of this with zcash this summer.

bought in march / early april and was giga bullish. then around the 400s i started seeing bear divs on the 2w and a possible one on the monthly, and talked myself into it going back to 300 or 200 and sitting there accumulating while majors ran. didn't want to sit in a big underwater position. traded in and out a few times, each one worse than the last, then bought back in anyway.

what i should have said to myself: zec was one of the strongest coins through the whole bear, and btc, eth and sol all had big bull divs on the weekly. the whole market going up while zec dumps off a chart divergence would be weird. maybe it underperforms, but more likely the bear divs just invalidate and it pushes through.

so if you're seeing htf bear divs on your coins right now after a run, or everyone's telling you it's some other chain's season, i'd zoom out and think about where we are in the cycle. there'll be pullbacks and a lot of volatility depending on what you hold. but if your thesis is intact, you think the cycle has more juice, and you still have conviction, trying to rebuy 25-30% lower is how i got chopped up. you don't know when it turns.

i'd just hold.

text:
JEV IS INSANE

your coding agents forget everything the second the session ends.

Every fix. Every dead end you already hit. Every "no, not like that."

Gone. Tomorrow you teach it all over again.

Someone just open sourced the fix, and it runs on Jev.

It's called Beacon, by @asymptotelabs.

It pulls in your session history from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 20+ other agent tools and turns it into one shared memory.

But storing everything isn't the hard part.

Most agent runs are GARBAGE to learn from.

Failed commands.
Wrong turns.
One off hacks you'd never want repeated.

Save all of that and your agent just gets confidently worse.

So Beacon keeps the full history, and Jev decides what actually earns a spot in memory.

Promote it.
Send it for review.
Or throw it away.

That's a decision you need on thousands of sessions, which is exactly why it has to be cheap.

The runs that survive get turned into reusable skills.

So something Cursor figured out on Monday shows up in your Claude Code session on Tuesday.

Your agents stop starting from zero.

Every good run makes the next one smarter.

quoted_text:
‼️New Paper Alert‼️What does it take to change behavior? In a fresh Annual Review article, @JGVoelkel, @AngelaDuckw and I argue it's helpful to consider 3 phases of change: 
1️⃣ building motivation
2️⃣ following-through
3️⃣ forming durable habits 

🧩KEY TAKEAWAY: At each phase, different obstacles to change arise that need to be met with evidence-based, tailored solutions. 

For instance, at the follow-through phase, forgetting can disrupt change. But forgetting can be combatted by reminders or feedback. Impatience can also disrupt follow-through, but it can be addressed in part by making change more fun or providing access to commitment devices. These are not the only obstacles to follow-through, however, and different obstacles arise at the motivation and habit forming phases, which are best tackled with entirely different solutions. Table 1 from our paper (reprinted below) offers a summary of common obstacles to change and evidence-based solutions.

⭐Our review focuses on solutions supported by *high quality evidence*, particularly from field experiments with objective behavioral outcomes (e.g., grades, gym visits, hours spent volunteering). 

👀Take a look at our new piece in the Annual Review of Psychology: https://t.co/vIeK5OVR4Z

Huge thanks to our excellent editor @EliJFinkel. We're very grateful for support from @Wharton, @BehaviorChange, @Penn and @Cornell, which made this work possible.

author: Foresight_News
quoted_text:
🪂来看看 32% 比例的空投方案明确了什么？

先说市场最关心的空投。

Variational @variational_io  并首次给出了较完整的代币分配方案：

🔹32% 为创始分配，即按用户持有的 Variational 积分比例空投，TGE 时全部解锁；
🔹18% 进入生态储备，由 Variational Foundation 用于生态发展；
🔹50% 分配给团队和投资者，TGE 后锁定 12 个月，此后用至少 3 年时间解锁；团队与投资者各自所占比例将在 TGE 前公布。

这也解释了此前官方文档中「约 50% 代币将分配给社区」的表述：32% 创世空投加上 18% 生态储备，合计正好为 50%。

空投的基本计算逻辑可以写成：

个人获得的 VAR 数量= 个人积分 ÷ 最终有效积分总量 × 代币总量的 32%

官方同时规定，账户至少需要持有 1 个积分，并签署相应服务条款，才有资格领取；未被领取的创世分配代币将被销毁。

每周仍将发放 15 万积分，持续到 TGE。这意味着，如果用户的积分不再增加，而全网积分继续增长，其在 32% 空投池中的占比就会下降。

此前 Entropy Advisors 制作的 Dune 空投模拟器假设积分活动在第三季度结束、最终积分总量为 915 万，并模拟了不同 FDV 与空投比例下的积分价值。若 FDV 达到 10 亿美元，单个积分价格达到 37.84 美元。

现在 32% 的比例已经确定，但积分活动被延长至 TGE，因此 915 万不能再直接视为最终分母。模拟器中的「每积分价格」和「预计空投价值」仍只是情景测算，不是官方估值或兑付承诺。

Entropy Advisors 制作的另外一个仪表板显示，Variational 平台总地址数量有 18.95 万个，其中活跃地址数量有 12.33 万个。

代币价值捕获方面，Variational 最新公告称，计划将「进入协议金库的收入」全部用于回购并销毁 $VAR。需要注意，这并不等于 Omni 的全部收入都会回购代币。

目前官方文档显示，协议金库暂时获得 OLP（Omni Liquidity Provider）价差收入的 20%，且这一比例仍可能调整；具体回购频率、执行方式和代币用途也要等 TGE 前进一步披露。

“ 币安会客厅 ” 这一期，很荣幸请到"财经女侠"叶檀老师

我们聊了很多大家最近很关心的话题：婚前财产要不要公证？赞成AA 制吗？三金该不该买，感情里能不能谈钱…也聊到叶老师从 2014 年创业到今天，一路走来的心路历程和心态变化

这些内容，完整版出来之后欢迎观看💛

这篇我想先单独整理一个话题，因为它几乎是每个人都在问的：现在到底处在什么周期？该投什么？

听完叶檀老师的分享，我把她的核心观点整理了出来

一、一个时代在结束，另一个早已开始

如果说现在是康波周期的转折点，那结束的是什么？

叶檀老师的判断是：互联网时代，正在走向尾声。接棒的是 AI。而且它不是刚刚开始，是早就开始了。

她给了一个信号：在中国整体投资下行的背景下，规划中的 AI 相关基础设施投资是几十万亿级别，年均复合增速在 10% 以上。一枝独秀。

只要到 2030 年的规划不变，社会的财富和资源就会持续向这个方向倾斜。

但她特别强调了一句：这不代表现在投 AI 就一定赚钱。AI 里面也分细分板块，也有波动。

二、中国的周期，被压缩了

从 1978 年到今天，中国用 40 多年走完了制造业、基础行业、信息化。

别人上百年的周期，在中国被大幅压缩。

结果就是：切换极快，也极急剧。

她讲了一个朋友的故事。90 年代在大开发商做区域老总，跟投买了 100 多套房。

放在 2021 年最后一波疯狂之前，这是神话。

但如果一直拿到今天呢？尤其在三四线城市，连出租都难。没有现金流，还要持续投入成本。

资产，立刻变成了负债。

三、财富在换手，人性跟着周期变

同一时期，另一群人的感受完全相反。

一位年轻的高科技企业家，公司刚上市，钱多到不知道怎么花，买房子推倒重建当消遣。

房地产商觉得寒冬，科技企业家觉得遇上了前所未有的好时代。

叶檀老师的总结是：我们看到的是人性的变化，但本质上，是经济周期带来的财富变化，改变了人。

四、中周期：地缘政治正在给行业定价

长周期之外，还有中周期。国际形势的变化，会让某些行业突然特别好。

她举的例子是船舶。

这一轮船舶周期持续得比以往都长。原因很具体：红海航道受阻，船要绕道南非，有的船甚至被扣住动不了。

以前一家航运公司 3 艘船就能周转，现在要 6 艘。

周转周期变长，需要的船更多。从全社会看，这是一种浪费型的、无效的投资。但对船舶行业来说，就是持续的景气。

再看船运保险价格，今天上天，明天落地，根本没法定价。

谁说了算？在社交媒体上发帖的人说了算。这就是现在市场不一样的地方。

五、长周期还在，有一条线从没变过

那是不是长周期不存在了？

叶檀老师说不是。从 80 年代到现在，有一条主线始终没变：高端制造和高科技的发展。

只要是能赚钱的高科技企业，就能发展得很好。

六、萧条末期，一个极端分化的世界

她也没有回避现实。从制造业投资和就业数据看，现在的经济很差。即便是最好的大学，有些专业的毕业生就业已经很难。

她的判断是：传统制造业和部分消费行业，正处在萧条期的末期，在见底。

但伴随着新力量的出现，会有人很好过，有人很难过。

我们面对的，是一个极端的世界。近在咫尺，冷暖不同。

我的一点理解是，

周期不会告诉你该买什么。但它能告诉你，钱在往哪里流、风险在哪里积累。

房子可以从资产变成负债，一个行业可以因为几发炮弹重新景气。所有"确定"的东西，都有保质期。

叶檀老师在分享中多次强调，每个人擅长的投资工具不同、承担风险的能力也不一样，小额试错、量力而行🤜🏻🔸🤛🏼

text: It’s 5.30am where I am but I couldn’t sleep with anxiety over the fact that the Muslim Brotherhood party in Morocco, which banned my work and threatened to take me to jail in 2015 over mere paintings with the Star of David, might possibly come back into power.  The good news is that they didn’t win the majority. The moderate sovereignty-first party of Authenticity and Modernity (PAM), won. Phew! The bad news is that the Islamist PJD came second and its narrative jihadists are already actively rewriting the facts to make it look like the election was rigged. This is the same playbook they use everywhere and they have their Aljazeera vultures on stand-by ready to amplify and broadcast the Islamist narrative to the whole world.

نقول لكم واحد النبوءة وعقلوا عليها 
حزب بن كيران الاخونجي غادي يخسروا الانتخابات بفضيحة وماغاديش يرضاو وغادي يقولوا انها مزورة  وغادي ينشروا اشاعات على انهم متصدرين وانهم حققوا نتائج وحتى غادي يقولوا انهم فازوا ...وخا قبل عد الاصوات ..كولشي هادشي راه حرب نفسية باش يوجودا لما هو قادم ....يعني غادي يقولوا لك هما لي ربحوا وتسرقات منهم الانتخابات.  

وغادي يطالبوا الاتباع ديالهم بالخروج للشارع للفوضى ....
يعني اما حنا او الفوضى 
وهاد التهديد قاله بن كيران حتى للملك يا اما نحن او تواجه رياح.

وهذا اسلوب اخونجي بامتياز في الانتخايات يا اما يفوزوا هم او يتهموك بالتزوير ويهددوا النظام بالفوضى ومظاهرات الشارع.  

وهذا احد اسباب تغطية قناة الجزيرة القطرية للانتخابات المغربية وراه بدات كتقسم الشاشة من دبا وعيق البريق.  

نتمنى المغاربة يكونوا واعيين بخطورة المرحلة التي يمر منها المغرب ويقفوا وقفة رجل واحد خلف الملك ...لانه الاعداء ظهروا بسيوفهم والخونة لي معنا ظهروا علنا  وهما الكوفيين لي هما ورقة عند الكابرانات وخلفها اسبانيا ..
يعني  كيستخدموا غزة وفلسطين غير ذريعة باش يفشلوا اي قرار ملكي فيه مصلحة ومنفعة للمغرب.  وهما ورقة رابحة عند النظام الجزائري والاسباني . 

هما اقلية والمغاربة الوطنيين هما الاكثرية ..علاش كيبانوا ليكم بحال الى هما بزاف اول شيء لانهم منظمين ما تنساوش راهم تنظيم ...كيخدم بنظام.  
ثاني حاجة هي انهم الاف الحسابات على مواقع التواصل تدعمهم ومصدرها الجزائر وقطر وحتى اسبانيا ..كيدعوا انهم مغاربة وكيغرقوا المواقع بتعليقات على اساس انهم مغاربة باش يحسوا المغاربة انهم اكثرية. 
هاد الاسلوب نجحوا فيه  ف داكشي لي دارو ف جيل زيد 
نجحوا فيه فاش هاجموا احتضان المغرب لكاس افريقيا 
ونجحوا فيه فداكشي لي وقع فسبتة. 

المهم ...هو انه على المغاربة يكونوا واعيين بان هنالك حرب حقيقية تدار على المغرب مشاركة فيها الجزائر طبعا واسبانيا وقطر  
من الخارج ...من الداخل حصان طروادة ديالهم هما الكوفيين واليساريين ... واحد يضرب من الخارج والاخر يضرب الاستقرار من الداخل ...

وعقلوا فين قلتها ليكم ..غدا يخسروا الانتخابات لان المغاربة ما بغاوهم ...ولكن غادي يخرجوا يقولوا ليك تزوير لانهم بغاو اي حاجة يخرجوا بها للشارع ويضربوا استقرار البلاد..خدمة للكابرات ولاسبانيا ..لانهم ببساطة خونة.  

والخونة بحال السرطان يا استئصاله ..يا اما غادي يقتلك.
